However, existing RA studies generally assume instantaneous antenna reconfiguration, whereas mechanical rotation incurs non-negligible delay in practical deployment. To address this issue, we develop a rotation-delay-aware communication model for finite communication slots, where mechanical rotation directly reduces the time available for data transmission. This model reveals a fundamental tradeoff between the communication gain achieved through RA reorientation and the associated transmission-time loss. Accordingly, we formulate a rotation-delay-aware joint design of RA orientations and transmit beamforming to maximize the minimum effective transmission rate. For the single-user system, under a sufficient condition for strict concavity, the global optimum falls into one of three regimes: no rotation, partial rotation, and full rotation. A closed-form approximation is derived using a second-order expansion. For the multi-user system, we separate rotation-budget selection from fixed-budget max-min signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) optimization. An analytic-gradient zero-forcing (AG-ZF) algorithm is then developed for low-complexity joint RA orientation and rotation-budget optimization. The results show that explicitly accounting for mechanical rotation delay is essential for finite-slot RA-enabled UAV communications, and that the proposed designs effectively balance reconfiguration gain and transmission-time loss while achieving favorable effective-rate performance with low computational complexity.
tldr: The paper develops a rotation-delay-aware beamforming and antenna-orientation design for rotatable-antenna UAV wireless links, balancing reconfiguration gain against lost transmission time.
motivation: Existing rotatable-antenna studies assume instantaneous reconfiguration, but mechanical rotation consumes a non-negligible fraction of a finite communication slot, so the true tradeoff between rotation gain and transmission-time loss must be modelled.
method: The authors build a finite-slot model in which rotation time reduces the data-transmission window, then solve a max-min effective-rate joint design of RA orientations and transmit beamforming; the single-user case is characterized via a strict-concavity condition and second-order closed-form approximation, while the multi-user case uses an analytic-gradient zero-forcing algorithm with separate rotation-budget selection.
result: The analysis identifies three optimal regimes (no rotation, partial rotation, full rotation) for the single user, and the AG-ZF scheme achieves favorable effective-rate performance at low complexity for multi-user settings.
conclusion: Explicitly accounting for mechanical rotation delay is essential in finite-slot rotatable-antenna UAV communications, and the proposed designs effectively balance reconfiguration gain against transmission-time loss.

title: Compact Toeplitz Operators And The Geometry Of Fixed-Radius Averages
authors: Zhaoxi Zhang Pan Ma
abstract: ArXiv:2610.22893v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We characterize compact Toeplitz operators with bounded complex-valued symbols on the Bergman space of a bounded strongly pseudoconvex domain with [MATH] boundary. For any fixed [MATH], the operator [MATH] is compact if and only if the Euclidean-volume averages of [MATH] over Bergman geodesic balls of radius [MATH] tend to zero at the boundary. This answers Zhu's fixed-radius question affirmatively on the unit ball. On the polydisc [MATH], [MATH], averages over products of Bergman discs of fixed radii characterize compactness, whereas averages over genuine Bergman geodesic balls need not. For every sufficiently small fixed radius, we construct a bounded real-valued symbol, smooth in the domain, whose geodesic-ball averages tend to zero along every sequence approaching the boundary, while its Berezin transform converges to a positive value along one such sequence. Boundary scaling reduces the strongly pseudoconvex case to a uniqueness problem for fixed-radius ball averages on complex hyperbolic space. We prove the required uniqueness theorem under a sharp decay condition expressed in terms of a Busemann height function.
tldr: The paper characterizes compact Toeplitz operators on Bergman spaces via fixed-radius geodesic-ball averages of their symbols and resolves Zhu's fixed-radius question on the unit ball.
motivation: It addresses a natural question in operator theory: whether compactness of Toeplitz operators can be detected by local averaging over fixed-radius Bergman geodesic balls rather than by vanishing Berezin transform.
method: The authors use boundary scaling to reduce the strongly pseudoconvex case to a uniqueness problem for fixed-radius ball averages on complex hyperbolic space, and they prove the needed uniqueness theorem under a sharp decay condition involving a Busemann height function.
result: On bounded strongly pseudoconvex domains, compactness is equivalent to vanishing of Euclidean-volume averages over fixed-radius Bergman geodesic balls at the boundary, while on the polydisc the analogous characterization requires products of Bergman discs rather than genuine geodesic balls.
conclusion: The work gives an affirmative answer to Zhu's fixed-radius question on the unit ball, clarifies geometric subtleties on the polydisc, and constructs counterexamples showing that geodesic-ball averages can differ from Berezin-transform behavior.

title: Achievable Rate Region Characterization Of Rotatable Antenna-assisted Interference Channel
authors: Junran Pei, Guangji Chen, Qingqing Wu, Qiaoyan Peng, Wei Cai
abstract: ArXiv:2610.23067v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper characterizes the achievable rate region of a rotatable antenna (RA)-assisted multiple-input single-output (MISO) interference channel. We exploit the additional spatial degrees of freedom (DoFs) offered by the dynamic orientation of RAs to simultaneously enhance the desired signal and suppress interference, thereby significantly enlarging the achievable rate region of the interference network. To this end, we invoke the rate-profile technique to formulate a sum-rate maximization problem for jointly optimizing the transmit beamforming and the array rotation, subject to the practical mechanical constraints of the RAs. For the special case of a two-receiver scenario, we introduce the concept of subspace correlation coefficient to derive closed-form solutions for the optimal RA rotation angles and transmit beamforming vectors. Inspired by the insights obtained in the two-receiver special case, we propose an efficient two-step optimization framework to obtain a high-quality solution for the general multi-receiver case. In particular, the array rotation angle of each transmitter is optimized to minimize the leakage interference to non-associated receivers. With the optimized array rotation angles, the optimal transmit beamforming is obtained by invoking the second order cone programming based approach. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed solution achieves near-optimal performance and that integrating RAs effectively simplifies transceiver designs by enabling simple maximum ratio transmission (MRT) beamforming with negligible performance loss.
tldr: The paper characterizes the achievable rate region of a rotatable-antenna-assisted MISO interference channel by jointly optimizing transmit beamforming and array rotation angles.
motivation: Rotatable antennas provide extra spatial degrees of freedom via dynamic orientation, which can boost desired signals and suppress interference, enlarging the achievable rate region of interference networks.
method: A rate-profile formulation of sum-rate maximization is used with mechanical rotation constraints; closed-form solutions are derived for the two-receiver case via a subspace correlation coefficient, and a two-step leakage-minimization plus SOCP beamforming framework handles the multi-receiver case.
result: Numerical results show near-optimal performance, and RA integration enables simple MRT beamforming with negligible performance loss.
conclusion: Rotatable antennas simplify transceiver design while substantially improving rate-region performance in interference channels.

title: Quasi-Monte Carlo Based Meshfree Methods For Parabolic Equations On Parameterized Riemannian Manifolds
authors: Zhijian He, Zhiyuan Hui, Changtao Sheng, Bihao Su, Tao Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2610.23341v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop and analyze a randomized path sampling framework for the pointwise approximation of linear parabolic equations on parameterized Riemannian manifolds, treating both closed manifolds and manifolds with Dirichlet boundary. Based on the Feynman-Kac representation, we construct a parameter-coordinate retraction-based discretization, referred to as the p-Ret scheme, for the manifold diffusion generated by the uniformly elliptic operator, and use it to formulate the Monte Carlo (MC) and randomized quasi-Monte Carlo (RQMC) methods. We derive the local weak consistency of the p-Ret transition and first-order weak convergence of the temporal discretization on closed manifolds. For fixed [MATH], we show that RQMC sampling yields asymptotically faster variance decay than standard MC. On closed manifolds, the variance is [MATH] and, under additional regularity, satisfies the sharper bound [MATH] for any [MATH]. For Dirichlet problems, despite the discontinuities induced by numerical first exit, nested-uniformly scrambled Sobol' sampling attains [MATH] variance for any [MATH] under suitable regularity assumptions, where [MATH] denotes the nominal path-space dimension. More notably, we further develop an Array-RQMC strategy based on stepwise low-dimensional randomized point sets and a Hilbert space-filling curve that maps high-dimensional particle states to a one-dimensional ordering, and establish a variance rate of [MATH] under suitable assumptions. Numerical results demonstrate that both RQMC methods reduce variance and root mean square error (RMSE) relative to standard MC and remain effective for manifolds with intrinsic dimension up to [MATH].
tldr: The paper develops randomized quasi-Monte Carlo and Array-RQMC meshfree path-sampling schemes based on Feynman-Kac representations for pointwise approximation of linear parabolic PDEs on parameterized Riemannian manifolds.
motivation: Solving parabolic equations on manifolds numerically is costly with grid-based methods, so the authors aim for meshfree stochastic samplers with provably faster variance decay than plain Monte Carlo.
method: They introduce a parameter-coordinate retraction-based discretization (p-Ret scheme) of manifold diffusion, prove local weak consistency and first-order weak convergence, and combine it with nested scrambled Sobol' sampling and an Array-RQMC strategy using a Hilbert space-filling curve ordering.
result: RQMC attains faster asymptotic variance decay than MC (sharpened bounds on closed manifolds), and nested-uniformly scrambled Sobol' sampling plus Array-RQMC achieve improved variance rates even for Dirichlet problems with discontinuous first-exit indicators; numerics confirm reduced variance and RMSE up to high intrinsic dimension.
conclusion: Quasi-Monte Carlo meshfree methods provide an efficient, provably convergent alternative to standard Monte Carlo for parabolic PDEs on manifolds.

title: The LLM-Attacker: A Unified Red-Team Framework For Privacy Evaluation Of Split And Distributed Llm Systems
authors: Evangelos Pappas Georgios Politis
abstract: ArXiv:2610.22722v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Split language models keep input text on a client but send intermediate representations to a server. Attacks can reconstruct text from these messages. Comparing privacy evaluations is difficult when attackers see different messages, know different model weights or use different datasets and recovery measures. We present LLM-Attacker, a framework that records these choices and lets researchers check, compare and extend an evaluation. Compatible attacks reuse recorded messages, and their predictions are saved for independent scoring. The scoring rule requires a linked undefended reference before a defence can pass. Reports also identify attacks that remain untested. In a controlled GPT-2 experiment, adding gradients returned during training increased token recovery from 94.20% to 97.38% and exact-document recovery from 13.71% to 37.77%. The 95% interval for the token gain lay above the two-percentage-point threshold fixed before testing. This experiment is shared with a companion study; here, it tests how the evaluation responds to a change in attacker access. Further studies measure how corpus choice and compression defences affect recovery, compare an adapted published attack with its reference implementation, and test the measurement code. The framework reports implementation checks separately from measured attack effectiveness. Each privacy claim should state the attacker, dataset and scoring rule, report its controls and identify untested attacks.
tldr: LLM-Attacker is a red-team framework for standardizing privacy evaluations of split and distributed LLM inference by recording attacker access, datasets, and scoring rules so that token- and document-recovery attacks can be compared and reproduced.
motivation: Split inference keeps raw text on the client but transmits intermediate representations (and sometimes gradients) to a server, which leak information about the input; existing privacy evaluations are hard to compare because attackers differ in message access, model knowledge, data, and recovery metrics.
method: The framework logs attacker configurations, reuses and shares recorded messages across compatible attacks, saves predictions for independent scoring, requires an undefended reference baseline before a defence can be declared effective, and reports implementation checks separately from measured attack success.
result: In a controlled GPT-2 experiment, granting the attacker training-time gradients raised token recovery from 94.20% to 97.38% and exact-document recovery from 13.71% to 37.77%, with the 95% interval for the token gain exceeding a pre-registered two-percentage-point threshold; further studies probe corpus choice, compression defences, and reimplementations of published attacks.
conclusion: Privacy claims for split LLM systems should explicitly specify the attacker, dataset, and scoring rule, report controls, and note untested attacks, so that reported leakage is comparable and reproducible.

title: Aspire: Practical Batch Queries On Dynamic Encrypted Database With Full Leakage Suppression
authors: Hao Nie, Wei Wang, Peng Xu, Haoming Yan, Laurence T. Yang, Kaitai Liang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.23057v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Leakage-abuse attacks against encrypted database systems exploit semantic leakage and pose a severe threat to the confidentiality of plaintext data and queries. To address this problem, we propose a zero-leakage encrypted database that rules out leakage-abuse attacks, which fundamentally rely on semantic leakage. We first distinguish between two kinds of zero-leakage security. Ideal zero-leakage forbids the disclosure of any information beyond public parameters, whereas restricted zero-leakage additionally permits the leakage of metadata (such as database size and query timing). We show that restricted zero-leakage is sufficient to thwart leakage-abuse attacks and is achievable in practice. We then formally define adaptive restricted zero-leakage security and present Aspire, an encrypted database that satisfies this notion. Aspire integrates probabilistic batch code and minimal perfect hashing to support efficient batch keyword queries and dynamic updates while revealing only non-semantic metadata. Experimental results demonstrate the practicality and efficiency of Aspire, showing that Aspire can achieve an amortized query latency of less than 1.38 ms (7.53 s for a batch of 5461 keyword queries), with an amortized communication cost of approximately 2.95 KB (16.1 MB in total), on a [MATH] key-value pairs database.
tldr: Aspire is a practical encrypted database system that suppresses semantic leakage while supporting dynamic batch keyword queries.
motivation: Leakage-abuse attacks on encrypted databases exploit semantic leakage to compromise plaintext and query confidentiality, motivating stronger leakage suppression.
method: The authors define adaptive restricted zero-leakage security and design Aspire using probabilistic batch codes and minimal perfect hashing to enable efficient batch keyword queries and updates with only non-semantic metadata leakage.
result: Experiments show amortized query latency below 1.38 ms and amortized communication around 2.95 KB on a large key-value database.
conclusion: Restricted zero-leakage is sufficient to thwart leakage-abuse attacks and can be achieved practically for dynamic encrypted databases.

title: Time-Domain Data-Driven Loewner Reduced-Order Models For Electromagnetic Simulation
authors: Pablo Biurrun, Carlos J. Ramos-Salas, Luis D. Angulo, Valentin de la Rubia
abstract: ArXiv:2610.22624v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents a data-driven Loewner framework for constructing reduced-order models (ROMs) from time-domain electromagnetic (EM) simulation data. High-fidelity simulation of microwave devices can be computationally expensive, particularly when fine spatial discretization and long observation windows are required. The proposed method uses transient input-output data to construct Loewner and shifted Loewner matrices, from which a reduced descriptor realization is obtained through singular value decomposition (SVD). The resulting models are identified from a limited training window and used to predict responses over substantially longer time intervals, with prediction windows up to 50 times the duration of the training window. The method is formalized as an explicit, reproducible algorithm and validated against full-order simulations for four microwave structures: a substrate-integrated-waveguide filter, a frequency-selective surface, an evanescent-mode coaxial comb-line filter, and a diplexer. The results demonstrate the potential of Loewner-based identification to provide compact models of electromagnetic responses while reducing the need for repeated full-order simulation.
tldr: A data-driven Loewner framework is used to build compact reduced-order models of microwave electromagnetic devices from time-domain simulation data.
motivation: Full-wave electromagnetic simulation of microwave structures is computationally expensive, especially with fine discretization and long observation windows, so cheaper surrogate models are desirable.
method: Loewner and shifted Loewner matrices are constructed from transient input-output data, and an SVD-based reduced descriptor realization is extracted via an explicit, reproducible algorithm.
result: The ROMs, identified from short training windows, predict responses over intervals up to 50 times longer, validated against full-order simulations for a SIW filter, a frequency-selective surface, a coaxial comb-line filter, and a diplexer.
conclusion: Loewner-based identification yields compact and accurate electromagnetic models while reducing the need for repeated full-order simulation.

title: Pressure-Dependent Hcp-to-fcc Phase Transition Path Derived From Exact Lattice Summations Over Inverse Power Law Potentials
authors: Tage W. Maltby, Andres Robles-Navarro, Jonathan K. Hartlaub, Andreas A. Buchheit, {\o}ivind Wilhelmsen, Morten Hammer, Peter Schwerdtfeger
abstract: ArXiv:2610.22855v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the phase transition between hexagonal close-packed (hcp) and face-centered cubic (fcc) structures along the Burgers-Bain transformation path at pressures up to several hundred gigapascals. We consider a hierarchy of interatomic potentials, from [MATH]-Lennard-Jones potentials to extended Lennard-Jones two-body interactions in terms of inverse-power expansions and the Axilrod-Teller-Muto three-body term, alongside density functional theory (DFT) calculations for solid argon. For inverse-power potentials, free energies are evaluated through exact lattice sums and efficient integral representations based on generalizations of the Epstein zeta function to anisotropic interaction kernels, followed by lattice-parameter optimization. This methodology enables an accurate determination of the pressure-dependent Burgers-Bain minimum-energy path and the associated activation barrier for the phase transition. The transformation exhibits pronounced symmetry breaking connecting the Burgers and Bain paths, a feature confirmed by DFT calculations. At high pressure, the hcp-to-fcc activation barrier increases approximately linearly with pressure, owing to the dominant pressure-volume contribution. Including entropy and anharmonic effects yields excellent agreement with experimental temperature-dependent volumes up to the melting point. DFT results also highlight the increasing importance of many-body interactions under compression. Whereas two-body potentials predict that the path passes through the body-centered cubic (bcc) structure only at very high pressures, DFT generally predicts a pathway that bypasses bcc. The Axilrod-Teller-Muto term slightly reduces this discrepancy. Furthermore, DFT performs better at high pressures, where dispersion forces become less important.
tldr: The paper maps the pressure-dependent hcp-to-fcc transformation path in solid argon using exact lattice sums for inverse-power potentials and DFT.
motivation: Understanding the hcp-to-fcc transition mechanism and activation barrier under high pressure is important for predicting structural stability in compressed materials.
method: The authors evaluate free energies via exact lattice summations and Epstein-zeta integral representations for Lennard-Jones and inverse-power potentials, including Axilrod-Teller-Muto three-body terms, and compare with DFT calculations for argon.
result: The Burgers-Bain path exhibits symmetry breaking, the activation barrier grows approximately linearly with pressure, and DFT predicts a pathway that generally bypasses bcc, with many-body effects becoming more important under compression.
conclusion: The methodology provides an accurate pressure-dependent transition path and barrier, while highlighting limitations of two-body potentials and the increasing role of many-body interactions at high pressure.

title: On Strongly Coherent Confidence Envelopes For The False Discoveries
authors: Romain P\'erier, Gilles Blanchard, Guillermo Durand
abstract: ArXiv:2610.22601v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coherence is a long term notion in the literature of multiple testing. From FWER control multiple testing theory to confidence envelopes on the number of false positives, coherence is a desirable property for multiple testing procedures. However, we show in this article that coherence is not a sufficient property to ensure that a multiple testing procedure is nonimprovable via an interpolation mechanism. We introduce a new no- tion, the notion of strong coherence, which is a stronger property than coherence and ensures that a multiple testing procedure is nonimprovable via the interpolation mech- anisms considered in the literature. Finally, we provide a uniform improvement of the confidence envelope from Durand et al. (2020) that is computable in polynomial time and demonstrate the improvement on simulated data.
tldr: The paper introduces 'strong coherence', a strengthening of the classical coherence property for multiple testing procedures, and uses it to derive a polynomially computable, uniformly improved confidence envelope on the number of false discoveries.
motivation: Coherence is a long-standing desirable property in multiple testing theory, but the authors observe that it does not by itself prevent a procedure from being improved through interpolation, so a stronger guarantee is needed.
method: The authors define strong coherence formally, prove that it rules out improvement via the interpolation mechanisms in the literature, and construct a modified confidence envelope building on Durand et al. (2020) that is computable in polynomial time.
result: The proposed envelope is shown to be a uniform improvement over the earlier construction, with the gain illustrated on simulated data.
conclusion: Strong coherence provides a sharper theoretical criterion for nonimprovability of multiple testing procedures and yields practically computable improved false-discovery confidence bounds.

title: Distributed Optimization Over Simplicial Complexes Via Topological Dirac Synchronization
authors: Christian D. Rodr\'iguez-Camargo, Andr\'es F. Urquijo-Rodr\'iguez, Eduardo A. Mojica-Nava
abstract: ArXiv:2610.22628v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a distributed optimization framework for systems with higher-order interactions represented by simplicial and cell complexes. Specializing global topological Dirac synchronization to gradient flows of strongly convex local objectives, we show that the synchronized equilibrium coincides with the minimizer of the aggregate cost, without Lagrange multipliers, dual variables, or saddle-point dynamics. Orientation-equivariant convex terms and cell-dependent dimensional targets allow the optimal state to be nonzero, as determined by joint per-dimension optimality conditions. Our algorithm couples signals across dimensions through the Dirac operator: nodes interact with edges, edges with nodes and faces, and faces with edges, enabling information exchange beyond graph-Laplacian methods. In the isotropic case, a Master Stability Function analysis yields a necessary and sufficient condition for local exponential stability: the product of the directional coupling strengths must be below the squared ratio of the strong convexity parameter to the spectral radius of the complex. A weighted Lyapunov argument accounting for non-normal Dirac coupling establishes global exponential convergence at the same rate. Finally, we identify a topological admissibility condition ensuring invariance of the synchronization manifold and coherent convergence of cells to the optimum, with no counterpart in classical graph-based distributed optimization.
tldr: The paper develops a distributed optimization framework on simplicial and cell complexes using topological Dirac synchronization to reach the minimizer of an aggregate strongly convex cost.
motivation: Classical graph-based distributed optimization cannot capture higher-order interactions among nodes, edges, and faces; the authors aim to exploit topological Dirac operators to enable cross-dimensional information exchange.
method: They specialize global topological Dirac synchronization to gradient flows of strongly convex local objectives and analyze stability via a Master Stability Function and a weighted Lyapunov argument.
result: The synchronized equilibrium coincides with the aggregate minimizer without Lagrange multipliers or dual variables, and local/global exponential convergence is established under a coupling-strength condition.
conclusion: Topological Dirac synchronization provides a principled distributed optimization scheme for higher-order networked systems, with a topological admissibility condition that has no graph-based counterpart.

title: A Spectral Approach To Fixed Points In Product Spaces
authors: Wojciech Kryszewski Aleksander \'cwiszewski
abstract: ArXiv:2610.22666v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study fixed points of mappings on finite products of Banach spaces whose coordinatewise Lipschitz estimates are controlled by a nonnegative matrix [MATH]. Our main result states that, if every coordinate space has normal structure and [MATH], then every such self-mapping of a nonempty weakly compact convex set has a fixed point. The result is a direct generalization of the Browder--G\"ohde--Kirk principle. The proof combines classical nonexpansive fixed point theory with Frobenius normal form, passing successively to coordinate projections and invariant fibres. As preparation, the classical reduction of Perov's theorem to the Banach contraction principle through adapted lattice norms is revisited. Applications include a Dirichlet boundary value problem for systems of abstract second order differential equations and a periodic problem for ODE systems satisfying one-sided matrix estimates.
tldr: A pure functional analysis paper establishing fixed-point theorems for Lipschitz-type mappings on products of Banach spaces, with coordinatewise estimates governed by a nonnegative matrix.
motivation: The Browder-Gohde-Kirk fixed point principle for nonexpansive maps is limited to single Banach spaces; the authors aim to extend it to finite products of spaces where contraction is only coordinatewise and matrix-controlled.
method: Combining classical nonexpansive fixed point theory (normal structure, weak compactness) with the Frobenius normal form of the controlling matrix, the proof passes successively to coordinate projections and invariant fibres; Perov's theorem reduction via adapted lattice norms is revisited.
result: If each coordinate space has normal structure and the spectral condition on the matrix holds, every self-mapping of a nonempty weakly compact convex set admits a fixed point, generalizing the Browder-Gohde-Kirk principle.
conclusion: The framework yields applications to a Dirichlet boundary value problem for systems of abstract second-order differential equations and to periodic problems for ODE systems under one-sided matrix estimates.

title: A Note On The Non-wandering Dynamics In The $n$-fold Symmetric Products
authors: Ma\v{s}a {\dj}ori\'c
abstract: ArXiv:2610.23058v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a homeomorphism on a compact metric space whose non-wandering set consists of a single fixed point, while the induced map [MATH] possesses infinitely many (non-fixed) non-wandering points.
tldr: The paper constructs a homeomorphism on a compact metric space whose non-wandering set is a single fixed point, while its induced map on the n-fold symmetric product has infinitely many non-fixed non-wandering points.
motivation: The work addresses a dynamical-systems question about how non-wandering dynamics behave under passage to symmetric products.
method: It provides an explicit topological/dynamical construction on a compact metric space and analyzes the induced map on the n-fold symmetric product.
result: The constructed example separates the non-wandering behavior of the original homeomorphism from that of its symmetric-product extension.
conclusion: The result shows that symmetric products can introduce infinitely many non-fixed non-wandering points even when the base system has only one fixed non-wandering point.

title: Watanabe's Learning Coefficients In Item Response Theory
authors: Joe Suzuki, Takumi Ikejiri, Yuki Kurumadani
abstract: ArXiv:2610.23102v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the joint-parameter two-parameter logistic (2PL) model in item response theory, in which both item parameters and respondent abilities are treated as unknown fixed parameters. We first characterize its singular structure through the Fisher information matrix. The parameterization has an inherent scale indeterminacy; when all discrimination parameters are nonzero and the ability parameters are not all equal, its tangent direction is the only null direction and the quotient model is locally regular. We then classify the additional rank deficiencies caused by zero discrimination parameters and degenerate ability configurations. This classification separates the strata governed by a nondegenerate quadratic approximation from those requiring an analysis of higher-order product singularities. Under an asymptotic regime in which the numbers of items and respondents are fixed and the number of independent response matrices tends to infinity, we derive explicit local and global learning coefficients and multiplicities for every realizable true response distribution. The global formulas depend only on the true response probabilities, including cases in which some probabilities equal \(1/2\) or are constant across respondents. These results extend previous calculations restricted to nonzero true discrimination parameters and provide the quantities required for applying sBIC to the joint-parameter 2PL model. Key Words: item response theory; two-parameter logistic model; singular learning theory; learning coefficient; real log canonical threshold; Fisher information matrix; sBIC.
tldr: The paper computes Watanabe's local and global learning coefficients (real log canonical thresholds) for the joint-parameter two-parameter logistic model in item response theory, enabling singular-BIC model selection.
motivation: Learning coefficients for the 2PL model were previously known only under the restrictive assumption of nonzero true discrimination parameters; a full characterization is needed to apply sBIC to realistic joint-parameter settings.
method: The authors analyze the Fisher information matrix to characterize the singular structure, identify the scale indeterminacy null direction, classify additional rank deficiencies from zero discriminations and degenerate ability configurations, and derive learning coefficients via resolution of higher-order product singularities.
result: Explicit local and global learning coefficients and multiplicities are obtained for every realizable true response distribution under fixed item and respondent counts, with global formulas depending only on true response probabilities, including cases with probabilities equal to 1/2 or constant across respondents.
conclusion: The work extends prior learning-coefficient calculations to singular cases of the 2PL model and supplies the quantities required for sBIC-based model selection in item response theory.

title: Generalization Of Navascu\'es' $\alpha$-fractal Operator On Lifted Sierpi\'nski Gasket
authors: Gurubachan, S. Verma, V. V. M. S. Chandramouli
abstract: ArXiv:2610.23159v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The primary objective of the present article is to extend Navascu\'es' class of [MATH]-fractal interpolation functions ([MATH]-FIFs) from a Euclidean domain to a non-Euclidean domain. Precisely, we consider the lifted Sierpi\'nski gasket [MATH], which is a subset of the first Heisenberg group equipped with a (popularly known as the Heisenberg metric), and demonstrate the existence of the class of [MATH]-FIFs in the continuous space on [MATH]. Subsequently, we derive certain conditions on the parameters so that the same class lies in the H\"{o}lder space on [MATH]. Next, we extend the theory of Navascu\'es' [MATH]-fractal operator from the Euclidean space to the Heisenberg space, and we also report several properties of the same operator. Additionally, we discuss certain dimensional results of the graphs of the functions with respect to the Heisenberg metric besides the Euclidean metric. We also cover some of the dimensional preserving and the set-valued results corresponding to the dimension of the graphs of the functions.
tldr: The paper extends Navascués' alpha-fractal interpolation functions and fractal operator from Euclidean domains to the lifted Sierpiński gasket in the first Heisenberg group.
motivation: The authors aim to generalize fractal interpolation theory beyond Euclidean settings to a non-Euclidean metric space, specifically the Heisenberg group.
method: They construct alpha-fractal interpolation functions on the lifted Sierpiński gasket, derive Hölder continuity conditions, extend Navascués' alpha-fractal operator, and analyze dimensional properties of function graphs under Heisenberg and Euclidean metrics.
result: The paper establishes existence of alpha-fractal interpolation functions on the lifted Sierpiński gasket, gives parameter conditions for Hölder regularity, and proves dimensional and set-valued results for their graphs.
conclusion: This work develops a fractal interpolation framework on a Heisenberg-group fractal domain, but it has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Critical Cusp Cancellation And Analytic Response For A Bernoulli Random Interval Map
authors: Furqat Vafoyev Davrbek Oltiboev
abstract: ArXiv:2610.23180v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that the critical cusp exponent [MATH] admits [MATH] invariant densities in an explicit family of expanding full-branch interval maps. The usual estimates exclude this exponent because two zero-order coefficients in the second derivative of the transfer operator are individually non-integrable. Their signed combination, however, contains the factor [MATH] for a pure power cusp. We exploit its cancellation at [MATH] to prove a [MATH] Lasota--Yorke inequality and a spectral gap for the explicit family. We also identify a separate obstruction caused by an interior cusp value. As an application, a small Bernoulli probability perturbation between two fixed maps has a stationary density that depends real-analytically on the perturbation parameter in [MATH], with explicit formulas for all response derivatives.
tldr: The paper proves existence of invariant densities and a spectral gap for an explicit family of expanding full-branch Bernoulli interval maps at a critical cusp exponent, using cancellation of non-integrable terms in the transfer operator.
motivation: Standard Lasota-Yorke estimates fail at the critical cusp exponent because individual second-derivative coefficients are non-integrable, so the authors seek to exploit their signed cancellation to extend ergodic-theoretic results to this parameter regime.
method: They analyze the transfer operator's second derivative, show the singular coefficients combine with a cancelling factor for a pure power cusp, and derive a Lasota-Yorke inequality plus spectral gap; they also examine an obstruction from an interior cusp value.
result: A spectral gap is established for the explicit map family, and as an application the stationary density of a small Bernoulli probability perturbation is shown to depend real-analytically on the perturbation parameter with explicit response derivative formulas.
conclusion: The work resolves a technical barrier in the ergodic theory of cusp maps and provides analytic perturbation (linear response) results, but it lies entirely in pure mathematical dynamical systems.

title: Accelerated Born Series For High-frequency Strong Scattering By Weakly Non-radial Media
authors: Faouzi Triki Mirza Karamehmedovi\'c
abstract: ArXiv:2610.23428v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a practical method for accelerating the modified Born series for high-frequency Helmholtz scattering in one, two, and three dimensions. We consider bounded, nonnegative, compactly supported media, allowing small departures from radial symmetry in two and three dimensions. The method selects a single complex relaxation parameter using an approximation of the scattering operator's spectrum. Starting from precomputed eigenvalues for a constant reference medium, we estimate their evolution towards the prescribed radial profile. A leading-order Wentzel-Kramers-Brillouin (WKB) approximation reduces this spectral propagation to scalar nonlinear equations, followed by a first-order correction for the nonradial part of the medium. The estimated eigenvalues, together with a bound on the omitted spectrum, define a convex minimax problem for selecting the relaxation parameter. This spectral preparation is independent of the source and can therefore be reused for multiple scattering problems in the same medium. Numerical examples demonstrate convergence in strongly scattering cases where the scattering operator has spectral radius greater than one. Comparisons with direct integral-equation and finite-difference solvers assess accuracy, residual convergence, and computation time, and show computational savings at comparable accuracy in selected examples.
tldr: Presents a spectral-preparation strategy for accelerating the modified Born series solver for high-frequency Helmholtz scattering in one, two, and three dimensions for weakly non-radial media.
motivation: High-frequency strong-scattering Helmholtz problems are numerically demanding, and the convergence of modified Born series depends critically on the choice of a complex relaxation parameter.
method: Eigenvalues of the scattering operator for a constant reference medium are propagated to the target radial profile using a leading-order WKB approximation plus a first-order non-radial correction; the estimated eigenvalues and a spectral bound define a convex minimax problem that fixes a single relaxation parameter, reusable across sources.
result: Numerical examples show convergence even when the scattering operator has spectral radius greater than one, with accuracy, residual convergence, and runtimes compared against direct integral-equation and finite-difference solvers, yielding computational savings in selected cases.
conclusion: Source-independent spectral preparation makes the accelerated Born series practical for strongly scattering, weakly non-radial media, though the approach remains a classical wave-propagation numerical method.

title: Capital Costs Protect The Network: Mining Gap Dynamics In Proof-of-Work Blockchains Under A Stochastic Mempool
authors: Nail Akar Hasan Sel\c{c}uk K{\i}l{\i}\c{c}
abstract: ArXiv:2610.22451v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Proof-of-Work blockchains increasingly rely on transaction fees to keep miners engaged as block subsidies decline. An immediate outcome of this is that miners may sit idle at the start of a round until enough high-fee transactions accumulate in order to make mining worthwhile. This idle period is known as the mining gap. We model the high-fee transaction backlog as a Lindley-type recursion under a two-tier fee market and use its stationary distribution to characterize the mining gap. Under Bitcoin's difficulty-adjustment mechanism, the expected gap grows strictly with the hashpower active on the network and consumes the entire round as that hashpower grows without bound. A free-entry condition determines a unique long-run equilibrium hashpower. Capital cost caps the equilibrium hashpower and prevents the mining gap from occupying the entire round. We further characterize how the block subsidy, transaction fees, and operating cost shape the equilibrium hashpower and the mining gap.
tldr: This paper models mining-gap dynamics in proof-of-work blockchains using a stochastic high-fee transaction backlog and free-entry equilibrium analysis.
motivation: As block subsidies decline, transaction fees increasingly determine miner participation, and miners may idle until enough high-fee transactions accumulate to make mining profitable.
method: The authors model the high-fee transaction backlog as a Lindley-type recursion under a two-tier fee market and use its stationary distribution to characterize the mining gap, with a free-entry condition determining equilibrium hashpower.
result: Expected mining gap grows with active hashpower and would consume the entire round absent capital costs; capital costs cap equilibrium hashpower and prevent this outcome.
conclusion: Capital costs play a stabilizing role in PoW blockchain security by limiting equilibrium hashpower and mining-gap growth under fee-driven mining incentives.

title: Can Solarburst Go Silicon? A Systematic Analysis On Software Supply Chain Attacks For Vlsi Design Flows
authors: Fabiha Hashmat, Zeren Li, Santiago Torres-Arias
abstract: ArXiv:2610.22580v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An attacker targeting the software supply chain (SWSC) of VLSI tools can fully subvert the VLSI design pipeline through purely software level compromises. However, cur- rent literature on both SWSC and VLSI hardware security has not explored how software can be used to subvert the security of the VLSI design flow. In order to bridge this gap, this paper presents a systematic analysis of the vulnerable surface of VLSI from a SWSC standpoint. We carry this anal- ysis through three major activities. First, we did an empirical analysis of VLSI software suites, focusing on their software composition, security features, and tool interactions within the VLSI design flow. Second, we develop a VLSI-SWSC attack taxonomy model that links software supply chain at- tacks and their mechanisms to the VLSI attacks they enable, the design-flow stages they affect, and their resulting security outcomes, allowing us to identify 717 possible new attacks, including 60 high feasibility attacks supported by evidence collected in our empirical analysis. Third, we identify what possible security outcomes can be achieved by an attacker from these attacks and produce a comprehensive VLSI SWSC threat model. We evaluate the feasibility of the attacks identi- fied by our taxonomy across VLSI design stages and assess existing defenses to determine which attacks are mitigated and which remain unaddressed. In addition, we present case studies using a reference VLSI design flow consisting of open- source VLSI tools and highlight attacks identified through our taxonomy on the VLSI SWSC uniquely from a software perspective.
tldr: The paper systematically analyzes software supply chain attack surfaces in VLSI design flows, building a taxonomy of 717 possible attacks including 60 high-feasibility ones.
motivation: Prior work on software supply chain security and on VLSI hardware security has not examined how purely software-level compromises of VLSI tooling can subvert the design pipeline, leaving a gap in threat modeling for hardware design flows.
method: The authors empirically analyze VLSI software suites (composition, security features, tool interactions), construct a VLSI-SWSC attack taxonomy linking attack mechanisms to enabled VLSI attacks, affected design stages, and security outcomes, and evaluate attack feasibility and existing defenses, including case studies on an open-source reference flow.
result: They identify 717 possible new attacks (60 with high feasibility backed by empirical evidence), produce a comprehensive VLSI SWSC threat model, and determine which attacks are mitigated by current defenses and which remain unaddressed.
conclusion: Software-level supply chain compromises pose a substantial and largely unaddressed threat to VLSI design flows, motivating software-perspective security hardening of hardware design toolchains.

title: Exploring The Empirical Privacy Landscape Of Synthetic Data
authors: Zihao Zhao, Avi Schwarzschild, Casey Meehan, Katherine Lee, Zhili Feng, Dylan Sam
abstract: ArXiv:2610.22659v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Methods for training language models on sensitive data differ in how they balance capability gains against the risk of leaking private information. In this paper, we present a controlled comparison of data-level and training-level interventions for navigating the capability-privacy tradeoff on synthetic medical records with canaries to probe for leakage. Direct finetuning performs best on capability metrics but leads to the most privacy leakage, while DP-SGD reduces leakage at substantial cost to capabilities. Generating synthetic data from these records offers a more favorable balance, particularly when guided by a uniqueness-aware instruction to replace private details. Relative to naive paraphrasing, privacy-aware rewriting improves privacy protection across a variety of different rewriting models. We also find that more capable rewriting models generally reduce the risks of downstream privacy leakage, although held-out fit does not improve monotonically and increased test-time compute yields inconsistent gains. Overall, these results highlight privacy-aware rewriting as a promising direction for achieving a more favorable trade-off between capabilities and empirical privacy compared to other training-level methods, and our evaluation framework supports comparisons of future models and methods.
tldr: The paper empirically compares data-level and training-level privacy interventions for language models trained on sensitive medical records, including synthetic data generation and DP-SGD.
motivation: Training language models on sensitive data creates a capability-privacy tradeoff, and practitioners need evidence on which interventions best reduce leakage while preserving utility.
method: The authors conduct a controlled comparison using synthetic medical records with canaries to probe leakage, evaluating direct finetuning, DP-SGD, paraphrasing, and privacy-aware rewriting guided by uniqueness-aware instructions.
result: Direct finetuning achieves the best capability but leaks most; DP-SGD reduces leakage at substantial capability cost; synthetic data generation, especially privacy-aware rewriting, offers a more favorable tradeoff.
conclusion: Privacy-aware rewriting is a promising direction for improving the capability-privacy tradeoff, and the proposed evaluation framework supports future comparisons of models and methods.

title: On The (In)stability Of Adaptive Fee Mechanisms In Multi-Chain Systems
authors: Yifan Zhou, Jiang Xiao, Xuechao Wang, Ru Cheng, Shijie Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.23305v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: EIP-1559 has become the dominant transaction fee mechanism in permissionless blockchains, regulating scarce block space through an adaptive base fee. The design balances a trade-off between responsiveness to demand fluctuations and stability of long-term resource usage. On a single chain, this trade-off is well understood and empirically stable. In multi-chain systems, however, cross-chain flows introduce delayed economic interactions across otherwise independent fee markets. These interactions alter the control dynamics and create stability risks that existing models do not capture. Deployed systems have already polarized. Polkadot enforces conservative update rates, effectively disabling fee adaptivity and reverting the market to inefficient first-price auctions. Cosmos adopts aggressive update rates without formal guarantees. To fill this gap, we propose a control-theoretic framework that formalizes multi-chain fee markets as a nonlinear dynamical system with delayed feedback. We identify delay-amplified over-correction as the structural root of instability. Experiments show that cross-chain coupling erodes stability relative to monolithic blockchains, reducing the safe parameter space for base fee update rates by up to 84.8%. Moreover, instability propagates across chains, contaminating the otherwise stable peer chains. At Ethereum's update rate, which leaves a monolithic chain stable, the multi-chain system exhibits extreme load oscillation between full and near-empty blocks, with over half of all blocks at full capacity. Mainstream Cosmos chains already exceed their safe bounds under their default configurations, and the resulting load oscillation raises their block failure rate by an order of magnitude. Guided by this mechanism, we design a lightweight protocol-level mitigation that removes the over-correction and stabilizes dynamics in multi-chain environments.
tldr: A control-theoretic analysis showing that adaptive EIP-1559-style base-fee mechanisms become unstable in multi-chain systems due to delayed cross-chain feedback, plus a lightweight protocol mitigation.
motivation: Cross-chain economic coupling introduces delayed interactions between otherwise independent fee markets, creating stability risks that single-chain models miss; deployed systems like Polkadot and Cosmos have polarized into conservative or unguarded update rates without formal guarantees.
method: The authors formalize multi-chain fee markets as a nonlinear dynamical system with delayed feedback and identify delay-amplified over-correction as the structural root of instability, validating with numerical experiments across coupled chains.
result: Cross-chain coupling shrinks the safe base-fee update-rate parameter space by up to 84.8%, propagates instability to stable peer chains, and at Ethereum's update rate produces oscillation between full and near-empty blocks, raising block failure rates by an order of magnitude on mainstream Cosmos chains.
conclusion: A lightweight protocol-level mitigation that removes the over-correction restores stability in multi-chain environments, highlighting the need for delay-aware fee-market design.

title: Local Projected Controllability Of Nonlocal Continuity Equations
authors: Elena Goncharova, Nikolay Pogodaev, Maxim Staritsyn
abstract: ArXiv:2610.22550v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formulate and study the problem of local projected controllability (LPC) for characteristic solutions of controlled nonlocal continuity (transport) equations on the space of probability measures over a separable Banach space. The task is motivated in particular by self-interacting models in machine learning, whose action can be represented as controlled dynamics of the probability distribution over input data, while the actual output is given by a finite-dimensional vector of features extracted from the terminal distribution by a possibly nonlinear observation map. Given a fixed finite family of velocity fields which may depend on the transported measure, we ask whether the reachable values of the observable vector fill a neighborhood of its reference value. Our approach is to lift the transport equation in the space of measures to an ordinary differential equation on a Banach space of maps. This representation makes it possible to employ the machinery of Lie brackets developed for Banach manifolds, while the resulting sufficient condition for LPC can be formulated directly on the space of measures.
tldr: The paper studies local projected controllability for controlled nonlocal continuity equations on spaces of probability measures using a lift to Banach-space ODEs and Lie bracket methods.
motivation: The problem is motivated by self-interacting models in machine learning, where controlled probability-distribution dynamics determine a finite-dimensional observable vector.
method: The authors lift the measure-valued transport equation to an ODE on a Banach space of maps, enabling Lie-bracket controllability techniques for Banach manifolds and yielding a sufficient condition formulated on the space of measures.
result: They obtain a sufficient condition for the reachable observable values to fill a neighborhood of a reference value under a fixed finite family of measure-dependent velocity fields.
conclusion: The work provides a control-theoretic framework for projected controllability of nonlocal continuity equations, but it has no direct connection to quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Continuity Of Biaccessibility Dimension For Polynomials
authors: Yan Gao
abstract: ArXiv:2610.22870v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a polynomial [MATH] of degree [MATH], its biaccessible set [MATH] consists of angles whose external rays are smooth and land at a point receiving at least two smooth external rays. We prove that the function [MATH] is continuous on the entire space of degree-[MATH] polynomials. Therefore [MATH] gives a continuous extension of classical core entropy from the postcritically finite case to all polynomials of degree [MATH].
tldr: The paper proves that the biaccessibility dimension of the biaccessible set of a degree-d polynomial is continuous over the whole space of degree-d polynomials, giving a continuous extension of core entropy beyond the postcritically finite case.
motivation: Core entropy and biaccessibility dimension are well understood for postcritically finite polynomials, but a continuous extension to all polynomials of a given degree was lacking.
method: The authors analyze the biaccessible set of angles whose smooth external rays land at points hit by at least two smooth rays and establish continuity of the associated dimension function over the full parameter space of degree-d polynomials.
result: The function assigning the biaccessibility dimension to each degree-d polynomial is shown to be continuous on the entire space of such polynomials.
conclusion: As a consequence, biaccessibility dimension yields a continuous extension of classical core entropy from postcritically finite polynomials to all degree-d polynomials.

title: Acceleration Survives Heavy Tails And Generalized Smoothness
authors: Eduard Gorbunov Taha El Bakkali El Kadi
abstract: ArXiv:2610.23301v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish high-probability accelerated convergence guarantees for convex [MATH]-smooth optimization with unbiased stochastic gradients under heavy-tailed noise, assuming a central [MATH]-th noise moment bounded by [MATH], [MATH]. Such guarantees are known under classical [MATH]-smoothness, but extending them through localization over an [MATH]-radius ball may introduce an [MATH] factor. We avoid this dependence in two ways. First, a two-phase scheme uses to reach a low-curvature regime, after which clipped stochastic similar triangles () attains, with probability at least [MATH], [MATH] where [MATH] bounds the distance from the Phase-II starting point to a minimizer. Second, a modified deterministic weight schedule allows to start directly from the initial point, controlling the high-curvature transient before recovering acceleration. With the prescribed initialization, both approaches recover the classical accelerated rate, with [MATH] confined to an accuracy-independent transient, up to logarithmic factors. The two-phase analysis uses two coupled potentials to preserve the low-curvature regime despite momentum; the one-phase analysis controls the initial high-curvature regime using a modified version of the classical SSTM weight schedule.
tldr: The paper gives high-probability accelerated convergence guarantees for convex stochastic optimization under heavy-tailed noise and generalized smoothness.
motivation: Classical accelerated guarantees rely on light-tailed noise and standard smoothness; extending them to heavy-tailed gradients can introduce undesirable dimension or initialization factors.
method: It proposes a two-phase scheme using clipped stochastic similar-triangles and a modified deterministic weight schedule to control high-curvature transients.
result: Both approaches recover the classical accelerated rate up to logarithmic factors, with the heavy-tail parameter confined to an accuracy-independent transient.
conclusion: Acceleration can survive heavy-tailed noise and generalized smoothness without an unfavorable radius-dependent factor.

title: Explicit Oblique Inverses Of The Approximate Discrete Radon Transform
authors: Donsub Rim
abstract: ArXiv:2610.23363v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The approximate discrete Radon transform (ADRT) is a fast, hierarchical approximation of the Radon transform whose levels have explicit spectral decompositions, but its Moore-Penrose inverse, needed for data outside the range, has no closed form. We construct explicit left inverses of the ADRT, oblique projections onto its range, that are exact for every choice of their parameters and amplify noise by a constant factor relative to the Moore-Penrose inverse. Realized with polynomial filters on the butterfly structure of the levels, they are fixed linear maps of cost [MATH] for an [MATH] image, where [MATH] is the smallest singular value of the ADRT; with the measured growth [MATH] this is [MATH]. A hybrid that keeps the explicit inverse of the cross-quadrant level is cheaper and closer to the Moore-Penrose inverse. In compiled implementations both outperform a polynomial solver of the normal equations from [MATH] on, and their conditioning is traced to the aliasing of integer-sampled lines.
tldr: The paper constructs explicit oblique left inverses for the approximate discrete Radon transform, providing efficient fixed linear maps that approximate the Moore-Penrose inverse.
motivation: The approximate discrete Radon transform has explicit spectral decompositions, but its Moore-Penrose inverse lacks a closed form, which is needed for data outside its range.
method: The author builds explicit left inverses as oblique projections onto the transform range, realized with polynomial filters on the butterfly structure of the transform levels.
result: The inverses are exact for every parameter choice, amplify noise by a constant factor relative to the Moore-Penrose inverse, and in compiled implementations outperform a polynomial solver of the normal equations from small problem sizes onward.
conclusion: Explicit oblique inverses offer an efficient alternative for inverting the approximate discrete Radon transform, with conditioning traced to aliasing of integer-sampled lines.

title: Convergence Rate Of Stochastic Gradient Descent Under {\L}ojasiewicz Type Condition And Polynomially Controlled Noise
authors: Pawe{\l} W\k{e}grzyn
abstract: ArXiv:2610.23386v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Stochastic gradient methods are widely used for solving optimization problems in many scientific fields. Recently, their popularity has risen due to the increase in machine learning's prominence. Their convergence is often studied under the convexity assumption, which is too restrictive in modern applications. In this paper, we investigate the almost sure convergence rate and expectation under a {\L}ojasiewicz-type gradient domination condition. This framework includes both bounded and decaying noise, as well as noise with controlled polynomial growth. The obtained results extend existing convergence by allowing a broader class of noise sequences and explicitly capturing the effect of their asymptotic behavior on the convergence rate and applicability.
tldr: The paper derives almost-sure and expected convergence rates for stochastic gradient descent under a Łojasiewicz-type gradient domination condition with polynomially growing noise.
motivation: Convexity assumptions are too restrictive for modern machine learning applications, so convergence theory is needed for broader non-convex settings and realistic noise models.
method: Theoretical analysis of SGD iterates assuming a Łojasiewicz gradient domination inequality, with noise sequences that are bounded, decaying, or of controlled polynomial growth, using stochastic approximation techniques.
result: Convergence rates in both almost-sure and expectation senses are established, extending prior results to a wider class of noise sequences and explicitly linking asymptotic noise behavior to the achievable rate.
conclusion: The framework unifies and generalizes existing SGD convergence guarantees, clarifying how noise growth governs convergence speed and applicability.

title: Regime-Aware Coupled Orchestration Of Neural Operator Specialists For Multiphysics Dynamics
authors: Paolo Guida, Vijayamanikandan Vijayarangan, Hong G. Im, William L. Roberts
abstract: ArXiv:2610.22378v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Real-world physics often unfolds over a variety of characteristic lengths and time scales. These non-uniformities are among the main reasons numerical simulations remain expensive when used predictively on practical systems: the same computational domain can contain smooth transport, vortical structures, thin interfaces, reaction fronts, and rapidly relaxing regions. Neural operators are attractive surrogates for such problems. However, a single architecture is still expected to represent all these local behaviours with a single set of weights and a single inductive bias. In this work, we introduce the regime-aware coupled neural orchestrator (RCNO), a framework that learns to distribute and connect a library of local operator specialists in space and time. For every patch, an orchestrator builds a causal query from the current fields, neighbouring halo values, local regime features, patch identity, activity level, and case parameters. The nine expert embeddings exchange two rounds of query-conditioned message passing before an edge-biased cross-attention stage produces a dispatch distribution that can be evaluated sparsely. Local predictions are assembled into a global field and projected onto system-specific physical constraints. A seam-aware extension additionally learns residual corrections across internal patch interfaces. We apply the same orchestration architecture to two qualitatively different systems: reacting flow and Cahn-Hilliard-Navier-Stokes (CHNS) dynamics. The results show that useful operator specialisation exists across local regimes, that the advantage of conditional composition increases as the spatial decomposition becomes finer, and, on reacting flow, that explicitly treating patch interfaces improves continuity, PDE consistency, and rollout accuracy.
tldr: The paper introduces RCNO, a regime-aware orchestration framework that spatially and temporally dispatches a library of neural operator specialists to model multiphysics dynamics such as reacting flow and Cahn-Hilliard-Navier-Stokes systems.
motivation: A single neural operator architecture must represent highly heterogeneous local behaviours (smooth transport, vortices, interfaces, reaction fronts) with one set of weights and one inductive bias, which limits accuracy on practical multiscale simulations.
method: For each patch, an orchestrator builds a causal query from fields, halo values, local regime features, patch identity, activity level and case parameters; nine expert embeddings exchange two rounds of query-conditioned message passing, followed by edge-biased cross-attention producing a sparsely evaluated dispatch distribution, with a seam-aware residual correction across patch interfaces.
result: Useful operator specialisation emerges across local regimes, the benefit of conditional composition grows with finer spatial decomposition, and on reacting flow explicitly modelling patch interfaces improves continuity, PDE consistency and rollout accuracy.
conclusion: Conditional, regime-aware composition of neural operator specialists is an effective route to accurate surrogates for multiscale multiphysics dynamics.

title: Development Of A Particle Bhatnagar-Gross-Krook Method For Rarefied Monatomic Gas Mixtures
authors: Inchan Kim, Joonbeom Kim, Woonghwi Park, Eunji Jun
abstract: ArXiv:2610.22389v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Direct Simulation Monte Carlo (DSMC) method has long served as a reliable numerical approach for simulating rarefied and non-equilibrium gas flows. Its computational cost, however, increases rapidly as the flow approaches the near-continuum regime. This limitation has motivated the development of kinetic model equations that replace binary collisions with simplified relaxation processes. This paper presents a particle multi-relaxation unified BGK (UBGK) model for monatomic gas mixtures. The model retains pairwise species relaxation and determines the target velocity, temperature, shear stress, and heat flux by matching the corresponding production terms to those of the Boltzmann equation. A stochastic particle algorithm is developed. The model is implemented in SPARTA, and two validation problems are considered: homogeneous relaxation and a Mach 3 flow over a cylinder. In both cases, the UBGK solution reproduces the DSMC reference behavior, including species-dependent relaxation and non-equilibrium shock structure.
tldr: The authors develop a particle-based multi-relaxation unified BGK kinetic model for rarefied monatomic gas mixtures and validate it against DSMC in SPARTA.
motivation: DSMC is accurate for rarefied and non-equilibrium flows but becomes prohibitively expensive near the continuum regime, motivating cheaper kinetic model equations that replace binary collisions with simplified relaxation processes.
method: A multi-relaxation UBGK model retaining pairwise species relaxation is constructed by matching target velocity, temperature, shear stress, and heat flux production terms to those of the Boltzmann equation, then implemented as a stochastic particle algorithm in SPARTA.
result: For homogeneous relaxation and a Mach 3 cylinder flow, the UBGK solutions reproduce DSMC reference behavior, including species-dependent relaxation and non-equilibrium shock structure.
conclusion: The particle UBGK approach offers a computationally efficient alternative to DSMC for rarefied monatomic gas mixtures while retaining key non-equilibrium physics.

title: GPU-Accelerated Robust Ma--ris Pre-Optimization For Communication And Target Illumination
authors: Ho Viet Duc Luong Tran Le Dung
abstract: ArXiv:2610.22431v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Movable antennas (MAs) and reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) offer strong spatial control for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), but repeatedly adapting MA positions and RIS phases to each channel realization can be impractical. This letter develops a GPU-accelerated robust pre-optimization framework that jointly selects slow-timescale MA geometry and RIS phases and returns a reusable Pareto set balancing expected worst-user rate and transmit-side worst-target illumination. The illumination objective measures directional transmitted power rather than complete echo-detection or parameter-estimation performance. The proposed Regime-Aware Multiobjective Pre-optimization (RAMP) preserves regime-specific Pareto populations, regulates cross-regime mating using Pareto-survival feedback, and constructs a worst-regime robust archive. Numerical results demonstrate competitive robust Pareto quality against the considered evolutionary baselines while avoiding online physical re-optimization.
tldr: The paper proposes a GPU-accelerated robust multi-objective pre-optimization framework (RAMP) that jointly selects slow-timescale movable-antenna geometry and RIS phase configurations for integrated sensing and communication systems.
motivation: Adapting movable antenna positions and RIS phases to every channel realization is impractical, so a reusable, robust pre-optimized Pareto set is needed that balances worst-user rate against worst-target illumination.
method: The Regime-Aware Multiobjective Pre-optimization (RAMP) framework maintains regime-specific Pareto populations, regulates cross-regime mating via Pareto-survival feedback, and builds a worst-regime robust archive, all accelerated on GPU and compared against evolutionary baselines.
result: Numerical results show competitive robust Pareto quality relative to evolutionary baselines while eliminating the need for online physical re-optimization.
conclusion: RAMP provides a practical offline design tool for ISAC deployments using movable antennas and RIS, though the illumination metric captures only directional transmit power rather than full echo detection or parameter estimation.

title: Optimized Linear Multistep Methods For Stiff Problems
authors: Tyler Jensen, David I Ketcheson, Lajos L\'oczi
abstract: ArXiv:2610.22685v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We design and test several new optimized linear multistep methods for stiff problems. Each method is A-stable, implicit, and second-order accurate. We focus on achieving the smallest possible error constant while also ensuring that stiff modes are damped. We recover some known optimal L-stable three- and four-step methods, and provide new and improved five-step methods. We also develop new methods that are not L-stable but provide a prescribed rate of damping in the infinitely stiff limit. Variable-step-size formulae are also provided for some of the new methods. Numerical tests demonstrate that the improved error constants lead to improved accuracy.
tldr: The authors design and test new A-stable, implicit, second-order linear multistep methods for stiff ODEs optimized for small error constants and controlled damping of stiff modes.
motivation: Stiff differential equations require implicit methods with strong stability properties; existing multistep schemes leave room to minimize the error constant while preserving damping of infinitely stiff modes.
method: They derive optimized linear multistep formulas with minimal error constants under A-stability/L-stability constraints, recover known optimal three- and four-step L-stable methods, construct new five-step schemes with prescribed damping rates, and provide variable-step-size variants.
result: Numerical tests show the improved error constants yield better accuracy, and the new five-step methods outperform previous ones while maintaining desired stiff-mode damping.
conclusion: Optimized multistep designs offer practical accuracy gains for stiff problems, though the work is purely numerical analysis with no quantum information or thermodynamic content.

title: Rigorous Verification Of Period-doubling Bifurcations In Maps
authors: Jean-Philippe Lessard Olivier H\'enot
abstract: ArXiv:2610.22986v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a computer-assisted approach for proving period-doubling bifurcations in one-parameter families of maps [MATH] on [MATH]. We solve a square augmented system, called the period-doubling map, whose unknowns are the fixed point, the parameter, the right eigenvector attached to the eigenvalue [MATH], the left eigenvector with its eigenvalue, and the vector which describes the center manifold to second order. A contraction argument gives a solution close to a numerical approximation, at which the Jacobian is invertible. The determinant of this Jacobian factors into a simple expression, so that it is nonzero exactly when [MATH] is not an eigenvalue and [MATH] is a simple eigenvalue crossing the unit circle transversally. Apart from the sign of the cubic normal-form coefficient, computed afterwards, it remains to check with Gershgorin disks that no other eigenvalue lies on the unit circle. The method is applied to a [MATH]-mode Galerkin projection of the Kot--Schaffer growth-dispersal model, for which we prove a supercritical period-doubling bifurcation.
tldr: The paper presents a computer-assisted method for rigorously proving period-doubling bifurcations in one-parameter families of maps.
motivation: Period-doubling bifurcations are central to nonlinear dynamics, but rigorous computer-assisted verification in map families remains challenging. The authors aim to provide a constructive proof method with explicit eigenvalue and contraction checks.
method: They formulate a square augmented period-doubling map whose unknowns include the fixed point, parameter, right and left eigenvectors, and center-manifold vector. A contraction argument and Gershgorin disk checks verify transversality and isolate the bifurcation.
result: The method is applied to a 12-mode Galerkin projection of the Kot–Schaffer growth-dispersal model, proving a supercritical period-doubling bifurcation.
conclusion: The approach gives a rigorous computational framework for verifying period-doubling bifurcations in maps and is demonstrated on a concrete population-dynamics model.

title: A Class Of R\'enyi-based Concentration Metrics For Kolmogorov-Arnold Geometry In Multilayer Perceptrons
authors: Juan Carlos Fern\'andez, Asunci\'on Jim\'enez-Cordero, Jos\'e Francisco Paris
abstract: ArXiv:2610.23267v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The interpretability of artificial intelligence models has become a central concern, especially for black-box models such as multilayer perceptrons (MLPs). Kolmogorov-Arnold Geometry has recently emerged as a framework for analysing the internal representations of these networks, by examining how the hidden layer locally responds to changes in the input through the minors of its Jacobian. The degree to which a few of these minors dominate the rest, known as their concentration, has so far been measured with the Participation Ratio. Although this metric has useful properties, its maximum value depends on the size of the network, so a given value cannot be read as high or low concentration without reference to the architecture. To overcome this limitation, in this paper we propose the [MATH]-RC metrics, a family of R\'enyi-based concentration measures that compare the normalized magnitudes of the minors with the uniform distribution through the R\'enyi divergence of order [MATH]. All the metrics in the family are bounded between 0 and 1 regardless of the architecture, with 0 indicating that the magnitude is evenly spread over the minors and 1 that it is carried by a single one. Moreover, the metrics are non-decreasing in [MATH], and for [MATH] = 2 they reduce to an explicit transformation of the Participation Ratio. Computational experiments with single-hidden-layer MLPs trained on a synthetic dataset show the benefits of our proposal.
tldr: The paper introduces a family of Rényi-divergence-based concentration metrics (R-C metrics) for quantifying how strongly a few Jacobian minors dominate the Kolmogorov-Arnold geometry of multilayer perceptrons.
motivation: The existing Participation Ratio measure of minor concentration is architecture-dependent in its maximum value, so a given value cannot be interpreted as high or low concentration without knowing the network size.
method: The authors define metrics comparing normalized Jacobian-minor magnitudes against the uniform distribution via Rényi divergence of order alpha, and validate them in computational experiments with single-hidden-layer MLPs trained on a synthetic dataset.
result: All metrics in the family are bounded in [0,1] independent of architecture, are non-decreasing in alpha, and reduce to an explicit transformation of the Participation Ratio at alpha = 2.
conclusion: The proposed R-C metrics provide architecture-independent, interpretable measures of representation concentration in MLPs, improving on the Participation Ratio for analyzing internal network geometry.

title: Finiteness Of Planar Central Configurations Of Six Bodies For All Positive Masses: Part I, Exceptional-mass First Limits
authors: Zhicheng Tong Zhe Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2610.23329v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We separate the generic positive-mass finiteness problem for planar six-body central configurations from finiteness on exceptional mass loci. The Chang--Chen diagram enumeration has 117 graphs. The arguments below confine 40 first-limit diagram obligations to proper necessary mass loci. In particular, a direct function-field argument establishes the No.~66 mass condition for both zero and nonzero drift. We establish the algebraic reduction from an infinite positive family to a germ with an unbounded seven-product, and use the stated diagram rules and computational certificates to confine its mass vector to the union of these loci. Finiteness on the exceptional positive mass loci, the proposed subject of Part II, will be discussed in another paper.
tldr: The paper studies finiteness of planar central configurations of six bodies for generic positive masses, reducing exceptional-mass cases to necessary mass loci.
motivation: The generic positive-mass finiteness problem for planar six-body central configurations is separated from finiteness on exceptional mass loci, with the latter deferred to Part II.
method: The authors use Chang-Chen diagram enumeration with 117 graphs, function-field arguments, algebraic reduction, diagram rules, and computational certificates to confine mass vectors to proper necessary mass loci.
result: Forty first-limit diagram obligations are confined to necessary mass loci, including the No. 66 mass condition for zero and nonzero drift, and an infinite positive family is reduced to a germ with an unbounded seven-product.
