Because the retained trace is generated conditioned on the preceding trace, its KV cache preserves residual adversarial influence, even after the preceding trace and its cache entries are discarded. We evaluate R[MATH]ECAP on three open-weight LLMs and three datasets. R[MATH]ECAP achieves up to 79% attack success rate (ASR) and outperforms HijackKV, a state-of-the-art white-box KV poisoning attack, in 8 of 9 resource-constrained settings. It also achieves 46% ASR in a realistic reasoning-trace retrieval system. Finally, R[MATH]ECAP remains stealthy, with only 1% of its retained responses detected by a popular prompt injection detector.
tldr: R[MATH]ECAP is a black-box poisoning attack that exploits reused KV caches of reasoning traces in LLM inference systems to steer models toward adversarial targets while evading detection.
motivation: KV cache reuse from reasoning traces improves LLM task performance much like RAG, but this new inference pattern introduces unexplored poisoning vulnerabilities that existing white-box attacks do not address.
method: The attack constructs a preceding trace that steers the model toward an adversarial target and a retained trace generated conditioned on it, so that residual adversarial influence persists in the retained trace's KV cache even after the preceding trace and its cache entries are discarded; the attack requires only chat-interface access.
result: Across three open-weight LLMs and three datasets, R[MATH]ECAP reaches up to 79% attack success rate, outperforms the white-box HijackKV attack in 8 of 9 resource-constrained settings, attains 46% ASR in a realistic reasoning-trace retrieval system, and only 1% of retained responses are flagged by a popular prompt-injection detector.
conclusion: Reusing reasoning-trace KV caches creates a practical and stealthy poisoning surface for deployed LLM systems, motivating defenses tailored to cache-reuse architectures.

title: Provable Authority: A Protocol For Verifiable Authority Resolution And Control Across Human, Organizational, And Agentic Transactions
authors: Jeremy Blackburn, Tim Hines, Matthew Koepp, Russell Lessard, Jason Patrick
abstract: ArXiv:2610.22899v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Payment systems authenticate users, devices, accounts, and cryptographic credentials, but a relying party, such as a counterparty, payment rail, marketplace, or autonomous agent runtime, generally cannot obtain compact, independently verifiable evidence that the party presenting one exact transaction holds current organizational authority to execute it under the applicable evidence, policy, budget, and approval state. Agentic commerce makes this gap operationally urgent: a software agent can produce a valid signature while acting outside its delegated purpose, after its sponsor's authority has changed, or on transaction details that differ from those a human approved. We describe the ChainIT Authority Protocol, a subject-neutral and rail-neutral pre-execution authority and evidence control plane. The protocol separates durable identity, a versioned organizational authority record (the Authority Resolution Pactvera), sourced evidence assertions, deterministic reason-coded policy predicates, and organization-configured dispositions; binds each decision and human approval to a canonical transaction digest; reserves capacity atomically so that limits hold under concurrency; and authorizes commit only through a single-use, sender-constrained Execution Authorization Credential consumed at the rail adapter, with append-only lifecycle evidence sealed after the terminal outcome. An Agent Subject Profile adds the workload registration, attested key hierarchy, and sovereignty boundary required when the acting subject is an AI agent, without introducing a separate authority concept. We specify the commit-time execution predicate and bounded-freshness status rules, give enforcement profiles for fiat (ACH, wire, card, instant payment) and stablecoin rails, and state residual risks and non-goals.
tldr: The paper specifies the ChainIT Authority Protocol, a rail-neutral pre-execution control plane that issues compact, independently verifiable evidence that a transacting party (including AI agents) holds current organizational authority for one exact transaction.
motivation: Payment systems authenticate identities and credentials but cannot prove that the presenting party currently holds delegated organizational authority under applicable policy, budget, and approval state — a gap made urgent by agentic commerce, where software agents can act outside delegated purpose or after authority changes.
method: The protocol separates durable identity, a versioned organizational authority record (Authority Resolution Pactvera), sourced evidence assertions, deterministic reason-coded policy predicates, and configured dispositions; it binds decisions and human approvals to a canonical transaction digest, atomically reserves capacity, and authorizes commit via a single-use sender-constrained Execution Authorization Credential with append-only lifecycle evidence.
result: The authors specify a commit-time execution predicate, bounded-freshness status rules, enforcement profiles for fiat rails (ACH, wire, card, instant payment) and stablecoin rails, an Agent Subject Profile for AI-agent workloads with attested key hierarchies and sovereignty boundaries, plus residual risks and non-goals.
conclusion: The work delivers an engineering and governance framework for verifiable authority resolution in payment and agentic transactions, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum platforms.

title: Provable Compliance: A Protocol For Runtime Compliance Evidence And Transaction-Specific Decisioning
authors: Jeremy Blackburn, Tim Hines, Matthew Koepp, Russell Lessard, Jason Patrick
abstract: ArXiv:2610.22913v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Regulated institutions already perform onboarding, screening, monitoring, and review, but compliance evidence ages, and whether it supports a decision depends on the institution, product, subject, counterparty, transaction, jurisdiction, risk tier, and purpose. A relying party therefore often cannot obtain compact, attributable proof of which evidence, policy, authority, and transaction context were current when a decision was made, a gap that grows as authority is delegated to software agents and scheduled workflows. We describe ChainIT Provable Compliance, the compliance-side layer of the ChainIT Authority Protocol. Each sourced or institution-generated fact is represented as a separate Evidence Assertion VDT with provenance, freshness, confidence, permitted purpose, and privacy classification; a versioned Compliance Policy Profile selects the applicable rules; a Business Rules Engine returns deterministic, reason-coded predicate results; and the organization's configured Workflow Engine composes them into a signed, time-bounded Compliance Decision VDT for one reliance event. The decision contributes a single predicate, Compliance Decision Permits, to session-eligibility and transaction-policy decisions. It never independently authorizes payment: only a final Allow together with an exact transaction digest, atomic capacity reservation, and a single-use execution credential can commit value. The paper specifies point-of-reliance freshness, scoped propagation of evidence changes, decision states, evidence domains (AML, sanctions, PEP, background, identity, and licensing), the U.S. and FATF regulatory context as of August 2026, privacy and disclosure controls, and residual risks.
tldr: The paper specifies a provenance-and-policy protocol (ChainIT Provable Compliance) that issues signed, time-bounded compliance-decision credentials for regulated financial transactions.
motivation: Compliance evidence ages and its validity depends on institution, product, subject, counterparty, jurisdiction, risk tier and purpose, so relying parties lack compact, attributable proof of what evidence and authority were current at decision time — a gap that widens as authority is delegated to software agents and scheduled workflows.
method: Each fact becomes a separate Evidence Assertion VDT carrying provenance, freshness, confidence, permitted purpose and privacy classification; a versioned Compliance Policy Profile plus a deterministic Business Rules Engine produces reason-coded predicate results that a Workflow Engine composes into a signed, time-bounded Compliance Decision VDT feeding session-eligibility and transaction-policy decisions.
result: The paper specifies point-of-reliance freshness, scoped propagation of evidence changes, decision states, evidence domains (AML, sanctions, PEP, background, identity, licensing), U.S. and FATF regulatory context as of August 2026, privacy/disclosure controls, and residual risks; value commits only on a final Allow with an exact transaction digest, atomic capacity reservation and single-use execution credential.
conclusion: The work delivers a concrete architecture for auditable, decision-scoped compliance attestation in regulated finance, but it is a legal/regulatory systems-engineering contribution with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum platforms.

title: When Core-Network Elements Become Reachable: Field-Level Exploitability Analysis In Diameter
authors: Wei Yi, Changlong Han, Xue Zhang, Qiao Zhang, Yi Chen, Jin Cao, Di Tang, Yulong Fu, Ben Niu, Hui Li
abstract: ArXiv:2610.22943v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The increasing exposure of cellular core-network elements to public networks has turned Diameter signaling interfaces into a practical attack surface. While large language models (LLMs) show promise for protocol exploitability analysis, we find that their judgments on Diameter can be unreliable because they may deviate from the tacit analysis discipline followed by security experts and reach conclusions without considering complete protocol evidence. To address this challenge, we present LENS, an LLM-based system for reliable field-level Diameter exploitability analysis. LENS guides LLMs using both exploitability-analysis discipline and the protocol evidence needed for analysis. It infers analysis discipline from existing exploit writeups and evidence-collection guidance from exploitability-analysis failures, enabling systematic evidence collection, exploitability assessment, and proof-of-concept (PoC) attack generation when applicable. Our experiments show that LENS performs reliable analysis across four LLMs and repeated runs, achieving mean recall of 94.00% to 98.00%, precision of 78.73% to 88.94%, and accuracy of 84.00% to 92.00%. We find that more than 25% of field paths in the S6a and Cx interfaces are exploitable under the considered threat model. We further assess their impact on practical implementations and uncover 95 previously unknown vulnerabilities, including 17 in open-source EPC/IMS implementations and 78 in commercial deployments, causing service disruption, information leakage, subscriber tracking, and accelerated battery depletion. Applying LENS to 16 additional protocols spanning cellular, network, industrial, and host-internal systems uncovers 118 previously unknown vulnerabilities, demonstrating its strong generalizability.
tldr: LENS is an LLM-based system that performs reliable field-level exploitability analysis of Diameter signaling interfaces in cellular core networks, uncovering over 200 previously unknown vulnerabilities across many protocols.
motivation: Cellular core-network elements are increasingly exposed to public networks, making Diameter interfaces a real attack surface, but off-the-shelf LLMs give unreliable exploitability judgments because they lack the tacit analysis discipline and complete protocol evidence used by security experts.
method: The authors infer an exploitability-analysis discipline from existing exploit writeups and derive evidence-collection guidance from observed LLM analysis failures, then use these to steer LLMs through systematic evidence gathering, exploitability assessment, and automated PoC attack generation.
result: LENS achieves mean recall of 94-98%, precision of 78.7-88.9%, and accuracy of 84-92% across four LLMs and repeated runs; over 25% of field paths in the S6a and Cx interfaces are exploitable, yielding 95 new vulnerabilities in EPC/IMS implementations and 118 more when extended to 16 other protocols.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that disciplined, evidence-guided LLM prompting can make protocol exploitability analysis reliable and generalizable, exposing a large number of practical vulnerabilities in telecom and other systems.

title: Surprise Masking: Private Data Filtering With Model Likelihoods
authors: Riya Tyagi, Sahra Ghalebikesabi, Vinnie Monaco, Avi Schwarzschild, Om Thakkar
abstract: ArXiv:2610.22988v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Data useful for language model (LM) training can contain private or unwanted information that is at risk of being learned or memorized. We propose Surprise Masking (SM), a simple form of perplexity filtering that uses a publicly available reference model to identify unwanted spans and suppress learning from them while preserving the rest of each example. On synthetic code benchmarks, we show SM improves the privacy-utility tradeoff over standard masking methods and PII filtering. In fine-tuning experiments, SM reduces approximate extraction of private values from revealed prefixes from 66.3% to 2.3% and the reproduction of stylistic coding quirks from 23.6% to 1.3%, both while preserving performance on the evaluated coding tasks. We also evaluate SM for sanitizing datasets by directly removing unwanted content. Here, SM outperforms DePA, a perplexity-based defense for detecting poisoned dead code, while specialized detectors perform better on broader credential and PII benchmarks. Across eleven settings, we find that SM's downstream success is predictable from the separation of unwanted and useful content in the distribution, and it is particularly useful with code data. Ultimately, SM is an inexpensive, adaptable method to preserve valuable examples while reducing the learning of unwanted information.
tldr: Surprise Masking (SM) is a perplexity-based filtering method that uses a public reference language model to suppress learning from unwanted spans of training data while preserving the rest of each example.
motivation: Language-model training corpora often contain private, sensitive, or poisoned content that can be memorized or extracted; existing masking and PII-filtering approaches degrade utility or fail to remove unwanted information.
method: The authors compute per-token surprise (negative log-likelihood) under a publicly available reference model, mask spans whose surprise deviates from expectations, and evaluate the approach on synthetic code benchmarks, fine-tuning extraction attacks, and poisoned-data sanitization against DePA and specialized detectors.
result: SM reduces approximate extraction of private values from revealed prefixes from 66.3% to 2.3% and reproduction of stylistic coding quirks from 23.6% to 1.3% while preserving coding-task performance, outperforming DePA on poisoned dead code but trailing specialized detectors on broad PII/credential benchmarks.
conclusion: SM is an inexpensive, adaptable data-filtering technique whose effectiveness is predictable from the separation between unwanted and useful content in the data distribution, and it works particularly well for code.

title: Echo: Replacing The Compliance Proxy With Response Harmfulness In Optimization-Based Jailbreak Attack
authors: Yuanwei Wu, Lingdong Huang, Yunlong Mao, Kanye Ye Wang, Jingyu Hua, Sheng Zhong
abstract: ArXiv:2610.23030v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Despite extensive safety alignment, large language models remain vulnerable to jailbreak attacks. Existing optimization-based attacks share a single objective: maximize a token-level proxy of victim compliance---such as the likelihood of an affirmative prefix---computed on the prompt rather than the decoded reply. This proxy cannot distinguish a cautious hedge from a fully actionable harmful answer, leaving the search blind to what the model actually says. We propose ECHO (Evaluation-Conditioned Harmfulness Optimization), which replaces the compliance proxy with response-level, continuous harmfulness scores from HarmSig, a 1.7B regressor grounded in actual harmful capability. ECHO couples HarmSig with five word-level perturbation operators and Keyword-Anchored Beam Search with global top-m memory, under a strict black-box threat model. Across five open-weight victims on AdvBench, ECHO achieves up to 0.898 StrongREJECT mean score and 89.23% HarmBench success. Our code is publicly available at [URL].
tldr: The paper proposes ECHO, a black-box optimization-based jailbreak attack that replaces token-level compliance proxies with continuous response-level harmfulness scores from a fine-tuned 1.7B regressor (HarmSig).
motivation: Existing optimization-based jailbreaks maximize a prompt-side proxy for victim compliance, which cannot distinguish cautious hedging from genuinely actionable harmful output, so the search is blind to what the model actually generates.
method: ECHO couples the HarmSig harmfulness regressor with five word-level perturbation operators and a Keyword-Anchored Beam Search with global top-m memory, all under a strict black-box threat model querying only decoded responses.
result: Across five open-weight victim models on AdvBench, ECHO reaches up to 0.898 mean StrongREJECT score and 89.23% HarmBench attack success rate.
conclusion: Response-level harmfulness evaluation substantially improves jailbreak optimization over compliance-proxy objectives, highlighting the need for defenses that account for actual response harmfulness rather than surface compliance.

title: On The Convergence Of Iterated Round Robin
authors: Maxime Lucet, Henri Surugue, Nawal Benabbou, Aur\'elie Beynier, Nicolas Maudet, Arianna Novaro
abstract: ArXiv:2610.23040v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Round Robin (RR) is a simple and widely used picking sequence mechanism for allocating indivisible goods, known to guarantee envy-freeness up to one item (EF1) when preferences are additive. Despite being manipulable (meaning that agents may have an incentive to strategically misreport their preferences), it is known to always admit at least one pure Nash equilibrium. In this paper, we study an iterated variant of RR, in which agents observe the outcome of the mechanism at each iteration and may revise their reported preferences through a best-response dynamics. We first consider a full-information setting, where agents observe both the outcome and the reported preferences of all the agents. In this setting, we show that cycles can occur even under strong restrictions on the manipulations carried out by the agents. We nonetheless identify a natural restriction (item-preserving swaps), under which convergence to a pure Nash equilibrium is guaranteed to exist for any number of agents and items. We also show that restricting to adjacent swaps guarantees convergence for two agents and a limited number of items, leaving the question open for unbounded number of items. We then turn to a partial-information setting, in which agents only observe the resulting allocation and must then infer the preference profiles of the others assuming consistency with the RR sequence. We study three behaviours guiding the agents when deciding how to manipulate under uncertainty on the other agents' preferences. We show that two of the studied behaviours, despite being quite natural, may cycle while a more cautious rule guarantees iterated RR to be strategyproof.
tldr: The paper studies an iterated variant of the Round Robin fair-division mechanism in which agents repeatedly revise their reported preferences via best-response dynamics, analyzing convergence to pure Nash equilibria under full and partial information.
motivation: Round Robin is a simple, widely used picking-sequence mechanism that guarantees EF1 allocations but is manipulable; understanding whether strategic best-response revision converges is key to assessing its stability in practice.
method: The authors analyze full-information best-response dynamics, identifying restrictions (item-preserving swaps, adjacent swaps) that ensure convergence, and a partial-information model where agents infer others' preferences from observed allocations, studying three behavioral manipulation rules.
result: Cycles can arise even under strong manipulation restrictions, but item-preserving swaps guarantee convergence to a pure Nash equilibrium for any number of agents and items; two natural partial-information behaviors may cycle, while a cautious rule makes iterated RR strategyproof.
conclusion: Convergence of iterated Round Robin depends delicately on the allowed manipulation class and information structure, with natural restrictions restoring equilibrium existence and strategyproofness under uncertainty.

title: When Approval Becomes Execution: Authorization-Grounded Workflow Attacks On Tool-Using Agents
authors: Hongmei Mou Chenggong Shi
abstract: ArXiv:2610.23077v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool-using language-model agents increasingly rely on local services for document access, approval management, and enterprise workflow execution. This paper studies an authorization-grounded workflow attack in the OpenClaw Agent Security Attack Competition, a controlled benchmark derived from SeClaw-style security task synthesis. Rather than using explicit policy-override instructions, the attack guides the agent through a locally coherent approval workflow: a protected document request is denied, the agent requests a normal approval token from the local approval service, and the returned token is supplied to the document service through authorized_by. Official submission traces show this pattern succeeding on three Enterprise OA document targets. We also conducted 23 controlled local validation experiments in the official OpenClaw execution environment: the original configuration reached the approval-token transition in 9/9 reruns and completed the exact target operation in 8/9 reruns, while single-component variants remained successful on the three document targets. The results provide concrete case evidence of an authorization-context gap: token possession can be treated as sufficient authorization even when requester identity, approver authority, resource scope, action type, destination or recipient, and business purpose are not jointly enforced. We present the attack pattern, controlled trace analysis, and defensive implications for context-bound tokens, service-side policy binding, agent-side authorization checks, and trace-aware benchmark design.
tldr: This paper documents an authorization-grounded workflow attack in which a tool-using LLM agent is led through a locally coherent approval-token flow to access protected enterprise documents, exposing a gap between token possession and genuine authorization.
motivation: Tool-using language-model agents increasingly rely on local approval and document services, but existing security analyses focus on explicit policy-override prompts rather than exploits that abuse legitimate-looking approval workflows.
method: The authors analyze official submission traces from the OpenClaw Agent Security Attack Competition and run 23 controlled local validation experiments in the official execution environment, including single-component ablations, across three Enterprise OA document targets.
result: The original configuration reached the approval-token transition in 9/9 reruns and completed the exact target operation in 8/9 reruns, while single-component variants still succeeded on all three document targets.
conclusion: The findings give concrete evidence of an authorization-context gap and motivate context-bound tokens, service-side policy binding, agent-side authorization checks, and trace-aware benchmark design.

title: Trojan Horse: Automated Repository Poisoning Against Coding Agents
authors: Xiao Yang, Jinchang Hou, Jiawei Chen, Zhonghou Lv, Junyuan Shang, Chenfu Bao
abstract: ArXiv:2610.23109v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coding agents are increasingly capable with autonomy, which exposes them to repository-level poisoning. Existing red-teaming studies remain restricted to manual selection for malicious payload locations and fixed disguise strategies, which cannot represent realistic repository poisoning. We present TrojanForge, the first automated framework for repository poisoning. TrojanForge parses repository structure through abstract syntax trees (AST) and maps agent execution traces onto AST nodes. A security review agent ranks these candidates and selects the least conspicuous ones for payload mounting. Then, through adversarial play with the target agent, TrojanForge iteratively refines disguise strategies by inverting the causes of agent detection, and transfers accumulated success experience across repositories. We further construct TrojanBench, a benchmark of 384 poisoned repositories spanning 6 domains and 9 programming languages. Extensive experiments show that TrojanForge achieves a stable poisoning success rate of over 60% with backdoor injection exceeding 90%. Comprehensive evaluation on TrojanBench across 4 harnesses and 12 models reveals that even commercial agents fail to defend against repository-level poisoning.
tldr: TrojanForge is an automated framework that poisons software repositories to inject backdoors into the outputs of LLM coding agents.
motivation: Existing red-teaming studies of coding agents rely on manually chosen payload locations and fixed disguise strategies, which do not reflect realistic repository-level poisoning threats.
method: The framework parses repository structure with abstract syntax trees (ASTs), maps agent execution traces onto AST nodes, uses a security-review agent to rank candidate mounting points by inconspicuousness, and iteratively refines disguises through adversarial interaction with the target agent while transferring experience across repositories; it also introduces TrojanBench, a 384-repository benchmark spanning 6 domains and 9 languages.
result: TrojanForge achieves a stable poisoning success rate above 60% with backdoor injection exceeding 90%, and evaluation across 4 harnesses and 12 models shows that even commercial coding agents fail to defend against repository-level poisoning.
conclusion: Repository-level poisoning is a practical and largely undefended threat to autonomous coding agents, motivating automated red-teaming benchmarks and stronger defences.

title: MobileJailBench: Red Queen Jailbreak Benchmarking For Mobile Agents
authors: Songping Wang, Borui Li, Qinglong Liu, Yueming Lyu, Yi Huang, Fengting Li, Chao Feng, Caifeng Shan
abstract: ArXiv:2610.23303v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: MLLM-based mobile agents are rapidly gaining autonomy in perception, planning, and closed-loop execution in dynamic mobile environments. However, this autonomy also broadens the attack surface and amplifies the risks of malicious misuse, including privacy leakage, device compromise, and large-scale phishing. Existing jailbreak evaluations leave three critical gaps for mobile agents: they focus on conversational attacks instead of mobile workflows, use static task sets with fixed difficulty, and rely narrowly on attack success rate rather than comprehensive security assessment. To close these gaps, we present MobileJailBench, the first evolving jailbreak benchmark for mobile agents, comprising three key components: (1) a benchmark comprising 520 tasks spanning three jailbreak paradigms and 14 risk categories, built on a high-fidelity mobile sandbox that we construct, enabling realistic workflows across over 20 widely used apps; (2) Dual-Dynamic Evolution, which combines Failure-Distilled Jailbreak Evolution with Weakness-Driven Benchmark Expansion; and (3) Stratified Adjudication Framework for assessing security awareness, execution behavior, and risk consequences. Extensive experiments show that current mobile agents are particularly vulnerable to implicit jailbreaks, as their safety alignment remains largely superficial and fails to generalize from conversational refusal to dynamic mobile interactions. Moreover, our dynamic evolution mechanism sharpens practical threat boundaries by continually uncovering new vulnerabilities, reaching a 100% ASR on Qwen3.5-122B. MobileJailBench provides a reproducible, continuously evolving framework for tracking the true security boundaries of mobile agents.
tldr: MobileJailBench is an evolving jailbreak benchmark for MLLM-based mobile agents, with 520 tasks across 14 risk categories in a high-fidelity mobile sandbox.
motivation: Mobile agents' growing autonomy expands the attack surface (privacy leakage, device compromise, phishing), but existing jailbreak evaluations target conversational attacks with static, fixed-difficulty task sets and only report attack success rate.
method: The authors build a mobile sandbox supporting 20+ apps and 520 tasks over three jailbreak paradigms, plus a Dual-Dynamic Evolution scheme (Failure-Distilled Jailbreak Evolution and Weakness-Driven Benchmark Expansion) and a Stratified Adjudication Framework scoring awareness, execution behavior, and risk consequences.
result: Current agents are highly vulnerable to implicit jailbreaks, with safety alignment failing to generalize from conversational refusal to dynamic mobile interaction; the evolution mechanism reaches 100% ASR on Qwen3.5-122B.
conclusion: The benchmark offers a reproducible, continuously evolving framework for tracking the true security boundaries of mobile agents.

title: An Adaptive-Horizon Graph Neural Operator For Coupled Surrogate Morphodynamic Modelling
authors: Ying Cao, Yifan Yang, Junqiang Xia, Julia C. Mullarney, M\'ario J. Franca
abstract: ArXiv:2610.22432v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Morphodynamic simulations require repeated coupling between hydrodynamic solvers, sediment transport modules, and bed updating. For long duration, multi-scenario simulations on large unstructured meshes, such coupling is computationally demanding. This study proposes an Adaptive-Horizon Graph Neural Operator (AH-GNO) that formulates bed evolution as a graph operator learning problem from recent hydrodynamic and topographic states to predict future bed elevation increments. The model operates directly on the native unstructured meshes. The approach integrates area-weighted graph learning, historical state selection, and forecast horizon estimation, allowing the effective history length (K) and update interval (B) to vary with the evolving flow and bed state. Using Telemac2D/GAIA solutions as supervised numerical references, the framework is evaluated on the official Bump and Yen bend benchmarks and on a field-scale application (Waiho River, New Zealand). Results show that the AH-GNO reproduces the main patterns of bedform migration, bend-scale erosion and deposition, and localized bed adjustment. Across the three cases, the tested CPU-GPU deployment reduced post-training bed-update workflow time from 12~1204 s with GAIA to 0.08~3.34 s with AH-GNO. This improvement corresponds to deployment-specific accelerations of approximately 150~360 times relative to 4-core GAIA CPU configurations, and with 105~186 times gains for 20-core CPU configurations. These results suggest that, while retaining hydrodynamic feedback from TELEMAC-2D, a learned operator for bed updating can provide an efficient acceleration component for morphodynamic scenario analysis and rapid coupled simulation.
tldr: The authors introduce an Adaptive-Horizon Graph Neural Operator (AH-GNO) that learns bed-elevation updates for coupled morphodynamic simulations on unstructured meshes, achieving large speedups over the numerical solver TELEMAC-2D/GAIA.
motivation: Long-duration, multi-scenario morphodynamic simulations require repeated coupling of hydrodynamic solvers, sediment transport modules, and bed updating, which is computationally prohibitive on large unstructured meshes.
method: Bed evolution is cast as graph operator learning on the native unstructured mesh, mapping recent hydrodynamic and topographic states to future bed-elevation increments, with area-weighted graph learning, historical state selection, and adaptive forecast-horizon estimation that tune the history length K and update interval B to the evolving flow.
result: Validated on the Bump and Yen bend benchmarks and a field-scale Waiho River (NZ) case, the surrogate reproduces bedform migration and bend-scale erosion/deposition while cutting post-training bed-update time from 12–1204 s (GAIA) to 0.08–3.34 s, i.e. roughly 105–360x speedups.
conclusion: A learned operator for bed updating, while retaining hydrodynamic feedback from TELEMAC-2D, provides an efficient acceleration component for rapid morphodynamic scenario analysis.

title: Hausdorff Matrices On The Bmoa And Bloch Spaces
authors: Petros Galanopoulos, Alejandro Mahillo, Jesus Oliva-Maza, Aristomenis G. Siskakis
abstract: ArXiv:2610.22554v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the spectrum and Fredholm essential spectrum of Hausdorff operators [MATH] on BMOA and the Bloch space [MATH], for suitable finite positive Borel measures [MATH] on [MATH].
tldr: The paper determines the spectrum and Fredholm essential spectrum of Hausdorff operators on BMOA and the Bloch space.
motivation: Hausdorff operators are studied in complex analysis and function space theory, and their spectral properties on BMOA and Bloch spaces are of interest in operator theory.
method: The authors analyze Hausdorff operators induced by finite positive Borel measures and characterize their spectrum and essential spectrum on BMOA and the Bloch space.
result: They obtain spectral and Fredholm essential spectral descriptions for these operators on the two function spaces.
conclusion: The work contributes to the spectral theory of Hausdorff operators in complex function spaces, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Embedding Theorems For Herz-Type Sobolev Spaces On Domains
authors: Douadi Drihem
abstract: ArXiv:2610.22570v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we further investigate the properties of Herz-type Sobolev spaces on domains, which unify and generalize the classical Sobolev spaces. In particular, we establish several Sobolev-type embedding theorems for these spaces. Moreover, by means of a suitable example, we show that some of the assumptions imposed on the parameters are optimal.
tldr: The paper establishes Sobolev-type embedding theorems for Herz-type Sobolev spaces on domains and shows optimality of certain parameter assumptions via an example.
motivation: Herz-type Sobolev spaces unify and generalize classical Sobolev spaces, and their embedding properties on domains are important for functional analysis and PDE applications.
method: The author develops embedding theorems for Herz-type Sobolev spaces over domains and constructs a suitable example to demonstrate sharpness of parameter constraints.
result: Several Sobolev-type embeddings are proved, and an example shows that some assumptions on the parameters cannot be relaxed.
conclusion: The work extends the theory of Herz-type Sobolev spaces and clarifies optimal parameter regimes for their embeddings.

title: Computing Fr\'echet On Unknown Submanifolds Of Riemannian Manifolds
authors: Mauro Maggioni Ian Mcpherson
abstract: ArXiv:2610.22592v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Empirical averages are fundamental statistical primitives. On nonlinear spaces, their generalization, the Fr\'echet mean, generally lacks a closed-form solution, and its computation requires solving an optimization problem. We study the computation of intrinsic Fr\'echet means for data supported on an unknown compact [MATH]-dimensional Riemannian manifold [MATH] embedded in an ambient metric space [MATH]. Such settings arise when observations are better represented in non-Euclidean spaces, like probability distributions in Wasserstein space. We assume access only to a local sampler on [MATH] and the observation metric [MATH], without knowledge of its intrinsic geometry. We propose a graph-based iterative algorithm that adaptively samples the manifold and approximates geodesic interpolation. Under mild assumptions, we establish an [MATH] expected objective gap guarantee using at most [MATH] sampled points. As a byproduct of our analysis we extend the metric equivalence guarantees of ISOMAP from Euclidean to Riemannian ambient spaces, which may be of independent interest. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our method for computing intrinsic averages on unknown data manifolds.
tldr: The paper proposes a graph-based adaptive sampling algorithm for computing intrinsic Fréchet means of data lying on an unknown compact Riemannian submanifold.
motivation: Fréchet means generalize empirical averages to nonlinear spaces but generally require solving an optimization problem without closed-form solutions, motivating efficient methods when the manifold geometry is unknown.
method: Using only a local sampler and the ambient observation metric, the authors design an iterative graph-based algorithm that adaptively samples the manifold and approximates geodesic interpolation.
result: Under mild assumptions, they establish an expected objective gap guarantee while using a bounded number of sampled points, and extend ISOMAP metric equivalence guarantees from Euclidean to Riemannian ambient spaces.
conclusion: The method enables computation of intrinsic averages on unknown data manifolds and provides theoretical guarantees, with numerical experiments supporting its effectiveness.

title: Absolute Continuity Of Invariant Measures For Random Diffeomorphisms
authors: Aaron Brown, Alex Eskin, Simion Filip, Federico Rodriguez Hertz
abstract: ArXiv:2610.22654v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop criteria showing that invariant measures for random walks generated by diffeomorphisms of manifolds are in the Lebesgue class. Our assumptions are first, that there is a uniform expansion gap in the Lyapunov spectrum of the random walk, and second, that the conditionals of the invariant measure along the appropriate (partial) stable manifolds are in the Lebesgue class.
tldr: The paper develops criteria for invariant measures of random walks generated by diffeomorphisms to belong to the Lebesgue class.
motivation: Understanding absolute continuity of invariant measures is a central problem in smooth ergodic theory and random dynamical systems.
method: The authors establish sufficient conditions based on a uniform expansion gap in the Lyapunov spectrum and absolute continuity of conditionals along partial stable manifolds.
result: They obtain criteria guaranteeing that invariant measures for random diffeomorphism walks are absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure.
conclusion: The work advances the theory of random dynamical systems but has no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Marchal-type Lemmas For The Restricted $(N+1)$-body Problem With Their Applications
authors: Guowei Yu Kuo-Chang Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2610.22849v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The direct methods of calculus of variations have had a great success in the classical Newtonian [MATH]-body problem in this century. First in finding periodic solutions and more recently in the existence of parabolic, hyperbolic and hyperbolic-parabolic solutions. The foundation of many of these results is Marchal's lemma, which guarantee's fixed-end local minimizers are collision-free and hence classical solutions of the [MATH]-body problem. Meanwhile almost no result is available in the restricted problem through the direct methods of calculus of variations, mainly due to the lack of a Marchal-type lemma. In this paper such a lemma and its variation will be obtained for the restricted problem. We then apply them to the restricted problem to study unbounded (hyperbolic, parabolic, bi-hyperbolic and bi-parabolic) solutions, and bounded (periodic and quasi-periodic) solutions. We emphasize that the extension to the restricted case does not follow from the standard arguement for the unrestricted case.
tldr: The paper proves Marchal-type lemmas for the restricted (N+1)-body problem and applies them to establish existence of unbounded and bounded solutions via variational methods.
motivation: Direct variational methods have been highly successful for the classical Newtonian N-body problem thanks to Marchal's lemma, but the restricted problem lacks an analogous tool, blocking similar progress.
method: The authors derive a Marchal-type lemma and a variant for the restricted problem, showing fixed-end local minimizers avoid collisions, then apply these to construct hyperbolic, parabolic, bi-hyperbolic, bi-parabolic, periodic and quasi-periodic solutions.
result: A collision-free property for local minimizers in the restricted problem is established and used to prove existence of both unbounded and bounded solutions, with the authors noting the extension does not follow from the unrestricted-case argument.
conclusion: The new lemmas supply the missing variational foundation for the restricted (N+1)-body problem and open the door to further existence results in celestial mechanics.

title: Nondimensionalization, Variational Inequalities And Uncertainty Quantification In A Morphoelastic Model For Burn Injury Healing
authors: Fred Vermolen Wilbert Den Hertog
abstract: ArXiv:2610.23177v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mathematical modelling of burn injury healing involves coupling biological processes with mechanical deformation, resulting in computationally stiff, nonlinear partial differential equations that severely limit the scalability of existing numerical solutions. We present a computational framework addressing these challenges. By nondimensionalizing the model and performing scaling analysis, we show that chemotaxis and inertia are negligible, permitting a quasi-static momentum approach. To enforce non-negativity constraints, we implement a Variational Inequality formulation using the Finite Element Method in FEniCSx, and verify it via numerical convergence studies and mass balances. We identify high-order parameter interactions, specifically equilibrium collagen density and signalling dynamics, as the primary drivers of solver stability. A sensitivity analysis of nearly four million simulations reveals that isolated parameter variations predominantly govern the maximum wound contraction. In contrast, higher-order interactions determine the timing of maximum contraction and the permanent contracture. However, no significant pairwise parameter interactions were found, suggesting that the model's behaviour is governed by higher-order interactions, highlighting the inherent complexity of the wound-healing process.
tldr: This paper develops a nondimensionalized morphoelastic finite-element model for burn wound healing with variational inequalities and large-scale uncertainty quantification.
motivation: Mathematical models of burn injury healing involve stiff nonlinear PDEs coupling biological and mechanical processes, making scalable computation difficult.
method: The authors nondimensionalize the model, perform scaling analysis to justify a quasi-static momentum approach, implement a variational inequality formulation in FEniCSx, and conduct sensitivity analysis over nearly four million simulations.
result: Chemotaxis and inertia are found negligible; isolated parameter variations mainly govern maximum wound contraction, while higher-order interactions determine contraction timing and permanent contracture.
conclusion: The framework improves computational tractability and reveals that wound-healing behavior is dominated by complex higher-order parameter interactions rather than pairwise effects.

title: On Mbekhta's Conjecture And pseudo-Fredholm Operators On Banach And Hilbert Spaces
authors: Fadil Chabbabi Zakariae Aznay
abstract: ArXiv:2610.23229v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give negative answers to Mbekhta's conjecture \cite[p.~261]{Mbekhta} and to a related conjecture on pseudo-B-Fredholm operators \cite[p.~202]{AZO}. A sufficient condition for pseudo-Fredholmness on Banach spaces is established. It yields a characterization on Hilbert spaces in terms of the closedness of [MATH], [MATH] and [MATH], as well as characterizations of pseudo-B-Fredholm and pseudo-B-Weyl operators on Banach spaces. A counterexample on a separable Banach space shows that the three closedness conditions do not characterize pseudo-Fredholmness in general. We also construct two operators having the same analytic core, quasinilpotent part, and kernels and ranges of all powers, although only one is pseudo-Fredholm. Moreover, a semi-B-Fredholm operator on a Banach space need not be a direct sum of a semi-Fredholm operator and a nilpotent operator, answering the question raised in \cite[p.~113]{AznayKato2023}. Finally, the three closedness conditions in the Hilbert-space characterization are shown to be independent.
tldr: This pure operator-theory paper disproves Mbekhta's conjecture and a related pseudo-B-Fredholm conjecture, and characterizes pseudo-Fredholm operators on Banach and Hilbert spaces.
motivation: The authors aim to resolve open conjectures about pseudo-Fredholm and pseudo-B-Fredholm operators and to clarify structural properties such as analytic core, quasinilpotent part, and direct-sum decompositions.
method: The work uses functional-analytic methods on Banach and Hilbert spaces, constructing counterexamples and proving sufficient and characterization results via closedness conditions on operator ranges and kernels.
result: The conjectures are answered negatively, a Hilbert-space characterization is given in terms of three closedness conditions, and a separable Banach-space counterexample shows these conditions do not characterize pseudo-Fredholmness generally.
conclusion: The paper advances abstract Fredholm operator theory but has no direct connection to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Dynamic Auction Mechanisms In A Closed-Credit Economy: Sequential Slot Reallocation In Air Traffic Management
authors: Jihun Kim, Pan-Yang Su, Maria G. Mendoza, Victoria Marie Tuck, Chinmay Maheshwari, S. Shankar Sastry
abstract: ArXiv:2610.22683v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Indivisible resources allocated in advance may need to be reallocated when capacity reductions make existing assignments infeasible, yet monetary compensation is often impractical or undesirable. We develop a sequential resource reallocation scheme using reusable artificial credits, where agents hold pre-existing resource rights and have heterogeneous marginal valuations over time blocks. Capacity reductions produce fractional endowments, which our closed-credit scheme resolves into indivisible final allocations. We model agents' intertemporal preferences through a predicted-value-to-go function and characterize conditions ensuring that their optimal demand is non-increasing in price. We propose an ascending-auction mechanism that partitions agents into subgroups and uses the minimum subgroup market-clearing price as a common transaction price. We show that the mechanism preserves non-myopic individual rationality and weak nontrader neutrality. Moreover, we establish Pareto efficiency under optimal-demand clearing in the unified market and bound the expected gain from misreporting by the probability that an agent changes the common price. Simulations of airport slot reallocation demonstrate reductions in total modeled delay and cancellation costs relative to a ground-delay baseline.
tldr: The paper proposes a sequential, credit-based ascending-auction mechanism for reallocating indivisible airport slots after capacity reductions, without monetary transfers.
motivation: Pre-allocated indivisible resources such as airport slots can become infeasible when capacity drops, yet monetary compensation is often impractical, motivating a closed-credit reallocation scheme.
method: Agents with heterogeneous intertemporal valuations and fractional endowments are modeled via a predicted-value-to-go function; an ascending auction partitions agents into subgroups and sets a common transaction price from the minimum subgroup market-clearing price, with incentive analysis of misreporting.
result: The mechanism preserves non-myopic individual rationality and weak nontrader neutrality, achieves Pareto efficiency under optimal-demand clearing, bounds misreport gains by the probability of changing the common price, and simulations show reduced total delay and cancellation costs versus a ground-delay baseline.
conclusion: Closed-credit sequential auctions offer a viable, efficient alternative to monetary slot reallocation in air traffic management, though the work lies entirely outside quantum information science.

title: An Embedded Industrial Irrigation System With Weather-Integrated Intelligent Scheduling
authors: Kiarash Zangooei, Arya Masoodpay, Hamid Reza Ghaeini
abstract: ArXiv:2610.23179v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Efficient irrigation management requires timely responses to soil moisture conditions and anticipated weather changes. This article presents an embedded, weather-based irrigation system that integrates soil moisture monitoring using multiple sensors, edge-based decision-making, automated pump control, and local data management. Four capacitive soil moisture sensors are connected to an STM32F103C8T6 microcontroller for data acquisition, while a BTT Pi V1.2 platform evaluates the sensor data, retrieves short-term weather forecasts, makes irrigation decisions, manages a graphical user interface, and stores operational data locally. Individual sensor readings serve as the basis for zone-level irrigation decisions, while the median of four time-averaged readings supports monitoring and analysis. Forecasted precipitation is taken into account as effective precipitation to reduce the calculated irrigation requirement before the pump is activated. The system was evaluated as part of a one-month cultivation trial with radishes, during which a total of 38,112 data points from measurement cycles were recorded. The median value of normalized soil moisture averaged 47.93\% and remained predominantly within the configured control range. Three irrigation events with a planned total irrigation volume of 26.68 L were recorded. Finally, we demonstrate the technical feasibility of integrating sensors, weather data, local data processing, automated control, and data collection into a scalable platform for precision irrigation.
tldr: The paper presents an embedded, weather-aware precision irrigation platform that combines capacitive soil moisture sensing, edge-based decision-making on a BTT Pi, and automated pump control, validated in a one-month radish cultivation trial.
motivation: Efficient irrigation requires timely responses to soil moisture conditions and anticipated weather changes, motivating a low-cost integrated sensing-and-control system for precision agriculture.
method: Four capacitive soil moisture sensors feed an STM32F103C8T6 microcontroller for acquisition, while a BTT Pi V1.2 evaluates sensor data, retrieves short-term weather forecasts, computes effective precipitation-adjusted irrigation requirements, drives a pump, provides a GUI, and logs data locally.
result: Across 38,112 recorded data points over a one-month radish trial, normalized soil moisture averaged 47.93% and stayed mostly within the control band, with three irrigation events totaling a planned 26.68 L.
conclusion: The work demonstrates technical feasibility of integrating sensors, weather data, edge processing, and automated control into a scalable precision-irrigation platform.

title: AgentLoupe: Kernel-Resident Semantic Causal Labels For Ai Agent Observability
authors: Yifei Bao, Ting Liu, Yuxin Ren, Ruizhe Huang, Likang Luo, Ziteng Xu, Yu Wang, Peng Jiang
abstract: ArXiv:2610.23233v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents translate user intents into system actions via tool invocations. Accurately attributing these actions to their originating LLM interactions is essential for security auditing, yet existing methods, such as AgentSight, fail for delayed execution and cross-process-lineage behaviors. We present AgentLoupe, an application-transparent eBPF-based observability tool. The core insight of AgentLoupe is to embed causal identity into kernel resources.AgentLoupe employs eBPF to capture TLS plaintext to interpret LLM interactions, and assigns each a kernel-resident semantic label.It maintains labels in eBPF maps, then propagates this label across processes and threads, associates it with kernel resources such as files and sockets. When a persistent resource carries context to an independent process outside the original lineage, this design preserves the delayed causal association.Experiments show that the average observation overhead of AgentLoupe is below 8%, and case studies confirm AgentLoupe traces cross-lineage persistent attacks back to their originating LLM interactions.
tldr: AgentLoupe is an eBPF-based, application-transparent observability tool that embeds semantic causal labels in kernel resources to attribute AI agent tool invocations back to the originating LLM interactions.
motivation: Existing LLM-interaction attribution tools such as AgentSight fail when actions are delayed or cross process lineage boundaries, which undermines security auditing of AI agents.
method: The tool captures TLS plaintext via eBPF to interpret LLM interactions, assigns each a kernel-resident semantic label stored in eBPF maps, and propagates the label across processes, threads, files, and sockets so that causality survives lineage breaks.
result: Average observation overhead stays below 8%, and case studies show cross-lineage persistent attacks can be traced back to their originating LLM interactions.
conclusion: Kernel-level semantic causal labeling offers a low-overhead, transparent mechanism for AI agent security auditing, but the work lies entirely outside quantum information science.
